advisor.10.desc:
We have found an §SAnomaly§!!

From time to time, our £science_ship£ §SScience Ships§! will make these discoveries while surveying alien worlds.

§SAnomalies§! can be researched by a £scientist£ §SScientist§!, if their skills are up to the task!

Unresearched §SAnomalies§! are listed under the §SAnomalies§! tab in the §SSituation Log§!. Some must be investigated before the £planet£ §SPlanet§! they were found on can be colonized or utilized.
advisor.10.name: Tutorial: Anomalies
advisor.15.desc:
One of our £science_ship£ §SScience Ships§! has just surveyed a world that would make an excellent candidate for our first £colony£ §SColony§!. It is of the same §Splanet class§! as our homeworld, so our colonists should be quite comfortable there.

Before colonizing this world, we must extend our borders.

With the £construction_ship£ §SConstruction Ship§! selected;

£dot_green£ Right-click a surveyed £system£ §SSystem§! containing a potential colony
£dot_green£ Select §S[GetBuildGrowCap] Starbase§!

$tttt$$ttt$£colonizable£

Once the §SSystem§! is claimed, we can begin the colonization process.
advisor.15.name: Tutorial: Colonization
advisor.17.desc: Congratulations on having colonized a new world! Our colonists are now in the process of building their first settlement, but it will take time for them to become self-sufficient.\n\nThe £colony£ §SColony§! will be a drain on our resources until the first settlement has been completed, so take care not to colonize too many £planet£ §SPlanets§! at once.
advisor.17.name: Tutorial: First Colony
advisor.2.desc:
Building a star empire can be a daunting task.

To help get things started, I will be providing instructional §SMissions§! that cover the basic steps necessary to establish ourselves as a successful interstellar power.

To access the §SMissions§!;

£dot_green£Click the §SSituation Log§! button on the left side bar or press §SF1§!

$tttt$$tt$£situation_log£
advisor.2.name: Tutorial: Situation Log
advisor.20.desc: We are losing £energy£ Energy Credits at an alarming rate. Last month's budget report makes for some grim reading.\n\nSpiraling upkeep costs are a common cause of budget deficits. If this is the case, we may want to consider disbanding some of our ships, armies or stations.
advisor.20.name: Tutorial: Negative Income
advisor.3.desc: Very well. I will provide tips and explain the basic functions of the various tools as you explore them.

akx.10000.a: Perhaps the Worm loves us, and perhaps we could love the Worm.
akx.10000.b: This is not a safe experiment. But we could learn so much.
akx.10000.desc: There is a consciousness outside time and beneath space. It is a labyrinthine tangle of desire and desperation. Our remote ancestors knew it as the Loop, the Worm-in-Waiting. We have met it out there, where the void is tormented by gravity. It seems to have taken a personal interest in us. There are mathematical proofs that it loves us, but love to the Worm is not like love to anything that subsists in ordinary space.\n\nWith all we have learned, we think that we might be able to use the Omega Alignment to open an access route - an Entry Point - for the Worm to manifest in our home system. (The Worm is fond of beginnings, and this is ours.) What consequences would that have? We have yet to find anyone who's prepared to commit to an answer. Immortality, perhaps, or apocalypse. But we would certainly learn a great deal.
akx.10000.name: The End in the Beginning
akx.10010.a: YES. Whatever it requires, we consent.
akx.10010.b: NO. We have brought it here to learn and, if need be, defeat it.
akx.10010.desc: The Project is complete. The accelerators are online. The power network of a dozen cities is diverted to wake the pseudo-singularity at the heart of the Alignment. Space shudders like wind-wracked cloth. [Root.GetStarName], for a heart-stopping moment, dims, and then brightens. A shadow coils in its heart. The Worm is here. It unfolds like origami.\n\nAcross the system, sensors shut down in abject disbelief as the incomprehensible data of its arrival sleets through them. On the homeworld, our subjects scream and cower as they feel its attention turned up on them, and upon us. It presents a wordless question - or rather, we have become aware that this question was always what it was asking us, every time we encountered it.
akx.10010.name: The Heart of the Sun
akx.10020.a: WHAT WAS SHALL BE WHAT SHALL BE WAS
akx.10020.desc: The Worm loves us. It will always love us, and thus it always has. It winds around the hot heart of our home star. It winds around every infinitesimal loop of information. It provokes a shuddering series of cataclysms in the planetary crust of our home, but when our star grows cold, that cataclysm will warm us. We understand so much more. We will always be what we were going to be, wound tight in the love of the Worm.
akx.10020.name: The Future
akx.10021.a: There are none like us! And perhaps there never will be.
akx.10021.desc: The Worm came in through the boundary fences of spacetime like a hungry predator, or a jilted and furious lover. It's still out there, and wherever it is, no doubt it's angry. But you have the incandescent shards of its avatar to hoard and to study, as a cosmic trophy. Other empires will know what you have achieved today.
akx.10021.name: The Shattered Loop
akx.9000.desc: An alert communications officer has identified what appears to be a faint signal, almost lost in the gamma-ray flashes from the black hole here - faint, but unmistakably artificial. This raises intriguing possibilities for our scientists.
akx.9000.name: The Horizon Signal
akx.9001.a: Fascinating! Send the vessel to those co-ordinates.
akx.9001.b: This is a trick, or a trap. Log it and move on.
akx.9001.b.tooltip: The techniques we developed to analyze the Signal will have some applications in Physics research.
akx.9001.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] reports that the signal was unexpectedly easy to decipher... but their team has spent considerable time confirming that it's not a hoax. It is a repeating, half-coherent message in the [Root.Owner.GetAdj] language - something like a poem. It repeats the phrases §HGRAVITY IS DESIRE§! and §HTIME IS SIGHT§!. It encodes co-ordinates near the black hole. And it ends with a dedication §Gby name§! to the Science Officer - who adds dispassionately that they have confirmed that the signal has been radiating into interstellar space since before their birth. In fact, the signal may predate our civilization.
akx.9001.name: The Horizon Signal: §HGRAVITY IS DESIRE§!
akx.9005.a.materialist: We learn, and we go on.
akx.9005.desc: As the [Root.GetName] approaches the co-ordinates specified by the signal, it begins to report spatial distortions and curious lensing effects - a rich stream of valuable data. Then the transmission becomes distorted. What happens next is analyzed exhaustively.\n\nThe excitement in Science Officer [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName]'s voice tautens to fear as the ship's hull struggles under increasingly exotic conditions. The ship triggers a distress call. [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName] cries out "the worm!" - or, perhaps, §Hthe Worm§!! Then all transmissions end. No trace of the [Root.GetName] is ever found - no further transmissions, no debris, and the space at those co-ordinates is innocuous and utterly free of distortions. But the data they sent back has advanced our Physics research dramatically. Perhaps it was worth their lives.
akx.9005.name: The Horizon Signal: §HTHE WORM§!
akx.9006.desc: [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName] complies with a mixture of reluctance and relief. Their cognitive report later indicates that they are subject to recurring visions - of impossible labyrinths, the hungry vertigo of interstellar space, and their name called in the dark. Within a homeworld year, the message has ceased.
akx.9006.name: The Horizon Signal: - message ends -
akx.9010.a.tooltip: §H[horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName]§! will arrive at the Exit Point in §Y30 days§!.
akx.9010.b.collective: Send them, but rig their ship's drive to detonate.
akx.9010.b.notcollective: Permit them to go, but rig their ship's drive to detonate.
akx.9010.desc: The black hole in [horizonsignal_system.GetName] is active again. Once again, a looping signal flickers in the darkness at the edge of normal space. But this time, there's an acoustic message encoded in the signal. It sounds very like [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName]'s voice. "What was shall be," [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName] intones, "what shall be was." Then the same co-ordinates as the first signal, the co-ordinates where [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName] was lost - what the media has christened "the Exit Point." Then they say a name: §G[horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName]§!.
akx.9010.name: The Horizon Signal: §HREPRISE§!
akx.9011.desc:
This time, the ship is running fully automated. [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] is the only crew-member aboard. As it approaches the Exit Point, the telemetry stream fills up with fascinating data. Once again, space flexes, gravity uncoils. [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] reads off the headline data, echoing the telemetry. They are commendably calm: we've sent a professional. It takes a little while for anyone to realize that something is peculiar about the timing.

[horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] is no longer echoing the data: they're predicting it. The telemetry disagrees, but only for a few seconds, until it catches up. The monitoring team is just reporting that the prediction interval is increasing when [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] says, wonderingly: "I'm through."

"It's dark," they add. "That's not a problem. We can live in the dark. I never thought of that. But of course, we can live here forever - if the Worm will only wait - "

At that moment, the signal cuts out, and the ship disappears from our team's sensors.
akx.9011.name: The Horizon Signal: I'm Through
akx.9012.a: And yet, this may not be the end.
akx.9012.desc:
This time, [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] is the only crew-member aboard. The ship is running fully automated... and its systems are programmed to detonate the drive once conditions match those immediately prior to the last ship's disappearance. As it approaches the exit point, the telemetry stream fills up with fascinating data. Once again, space flexes, gravity uncoils. [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] reads off the headline data, echoing the telemetry. They are commendably calm: we've sent a professional. It takes a little while for anyone to realize that something is peculiar about the timing.

[horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] is no longer echoing the data: They're predicting it. The telemetry disagrees, but only for a few seconds, until it catches up. Our monitoring team is just reporting that the prediction interval is increasing when there is a sudden energy spike.

The drive has detonated: a brief flare of stellar fury, quickly lost in the darkness of [horizonsignal_system.GetName]. Whatever we encountered there, it may regret its interference. We'll never know. The Horizon Signal does not come again. But our team may find something interesting in the ashes of the ship.
akx.9012.name: The Horizon Signal: An Intervention
akx.9013.desc: [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName] complies with obvious relief. Their cognitive report later indicates that they are subject to visions - of impossible labyrinths, of the hungry vertigo of interstellar space, of their name called in the dark. Within a homeworld year, the message has ceased.
akx.9013.name: The Horizon Signal: - message ends -
akx.9020.a.tooltip: §H[horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName]§! will arrive at the Exit Point in §Y30 days§!.
akx.9020.b: Send [horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName], with their drive rigged to blow.
akx.9020.c: This is sinister, and ridiculous, and sinister. Let it go.
akx.9020.desc: Once again, the Horizon Signal in [horizonsignal_system.GetName] is active. It has upped its game. Once again, the transmission includes the Exit Point's co-ordinates. It's signed with the private comm keys of [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName] and [horizonsignal_secondleader.GetName]. But this time, it's a generative text program written in an elderly programming language that creates what appear to be love poems - love poems directed to [horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName].\n\nThey're honestly not very good love poems. But it is, our scientists agree, quite difficult to generate love poems procedurally, and quite unusual for a black hole to send love poems at all.
akx.9020.name: The Horizon Signal: §HTHE TRINE THE QUINE THE TRINE§!
akx.9021.a: And yet, this may not be the end.
akx.9021.desc:
"This will be the end of me," [horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName] says at the briefing before launch. "I know I won't come back. But I think I always knew this would happen. Whatever is in the hole has been waiting for us for a long long time - I think it's been waiting for me, since before I was born."

Once again, the single-pilot ship approaches the Exit Point. Once again, space boils like a fever. Again, our sensor arrays soak up fascinating data. This time, [horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName] is silent. The telemetry becomes intermittent; and then it, too, is silent. The ship has reached the Exit Point. The conditions around it are returning to normal. Nothing has happened.

Nothing? The monitoring team mutter furiously. The ship is different... in fact, it's a different ship. It's [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName]'s vessel, lost these years past, drifting now away from the Exit Point. A salvage team finds it pristine and empty - no trace of crew, and no sign of violence. But there's a journal entry in [horizonsignal_firstleader.GetName]'s name, titled §HWHAT WAS WILL BE§!. Our scientists review it nervously. "Impossible," one says. "I hope so," says another.

The ship is renamed the "Foundling" and returned to service. The Signal, dead or sleeping, says nothing at all, ever again.
akx.9021.name: The Horizon Signal: Where the End Comes From
akx.9022.a: And yet, this may not be the end.
akx.9022.desc:
"This will be the end of me," they say at the briefing before launch. "I know I won't come back. But I think I always knew this would happen. Whatever is in the hole has been waiting for us for a long, long time - I think it's been waiting for me, since before I was born."

Once again, the single-pilot ship approaches the Exit Point. Once again, space boils like a fever. Again, our sensor arrays soak up fascinating data. This time, [horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName] is silent. The telemetry becomes intermittent...

And then the drive detonates: a brief flare of stellar fury, quickly lost in the darkness of the [horizonsignal_system.GetName] system. Whatever we encountered there, it may regret its interference. We'll never know. The Horizon Signal does not come again. But our team may find something interesting in the ashes of the ship.
akx.9022.name: The Horizon Signal: An Intervention
akx.9023.desc: [horizonsignal_thirdleader.GetName] complies with obvious relief. Their cognitive report later indicates that they are subject to recurring visions - of impossible labyrinths, the hungry vertigo of interstellar space, and their name called in the dark. Within a year, the message has ceased.
akx.9023.name: The Horizon Signal: - message ends -
akx.9095.desc: We've reproduced conditions that approximate those around the black hole. We've found that the fragments we recover cycle between states, in ways that should be impossible - as if time were oscillating. We can derive energy from this - although there are worrying changes to local spacetime.
akx.9095.name: The Horizon Signal: A Lesson in the Ashes
akx.9100.desc: Archaeologists have found a forgotten temple in the remote highlands of [Root.GetName] - buried for centuries, but recently exposed by an earthquake. Dating techniques suggest it's a pre-industrial relic, [Owner.Species.GetHandName]-hewn from volcanic rock. However, the recurring symbol on the walls and radial altar - a Möbius-looped serpent consuming its own tail - has no obvious precedent in our early history, and the inscriptions use an unknown alphabet. One excitable archaeologist suggests it's a relic left by an unknown precursor species.\n\nIn a presumably meaningless coincidence, the quake seems to have occurred at the same time as the final message from the black hole in [horizonsignal_system.GetName].
akx.9100.name: The Loop Temple: Signs in the Stone
akx.9100.spiritual.a: A way has been opened for us.
akx.9101.a.notspiritual: Open the Loop Temple to the public.
akx.9101.a.notspiritual.tooltip: Something from our past. What was, will be.
akx.9101.a.spiritual: Make the Loop Temple a place of pilgrimage.
akx.9101.a.spiritual.tooltip: A wisdom from the faith of our predecessors. What was, will be. Increases planet happiness, among other things.
akx.9101.b: Reserve the Temple for academic study only.
akx.9101.b.tooltip: Let's limit access to those who need it.
akx.9101.c: There is something wrong here. Seal the Temple.
akx.9101.desc:
Our scientists have learned a great deal about the subterranean temple, but some questions remain. A roof aperture - along with the radial altar - suggests it was once a solar calendar, but it's so badly damaged by the earthquake that we can't be certain. If the builders found any particular dates important, we'll never know which ones. We've had better luck with the "unknown alphabet." It's a debased variant of a better-known hieratic script - not an alien language at all - and we've successfully deciphered it.

The temple is dedicated to the "Waiting Worm" or the §HWorm-in-Waiting§!. Most of the inscriptions are sonorous, poetic invocations requesting its appearance or - if read in the other direction - its departure. There is also a body of inscriptions describing the "operations of the universe," which our more excitable archaeologist swears contains references to advanced field equations - nothing new to us, but very impressive for a temple of this vintage. We have yet to find a physicist who's prepared to go on record in agreeing that the references are meaningful, though.

The temple holds no cosmic secrets or alien weapons, as far as we can tell, but its dark spaces have a distinctive, menacing beauty - and the poetry of the invocations to the Worm-in-Waiting becomes fashionable. They are set to popular music; they are published in collections.
akx.9101.name: The Loop Temple: Time and Stone
akx.9200.desc: The [Root.GetName] has located a small, minimally powered artificial object, broadcasting a looping signal at local range only. These sorts of things usually turn out to be escape pods, and this looks like one of those. It's been out here a long time.\n\nWhen the crew cracks it open - carefully observing quarantine procedures - they find ancient remains, preserved by the sterile pod environment. So far, not unusual. The captain of the [Root.GetName] indicates, however, that they did not expect to find the [Root.Owner.GetAdj] words §HWHAT WAS, WILL BE; WHAT WILL BE, WAS§! daubed on the wall in the bodily fluids of the pod's occupant - who the crew are now wryly referring to as "the Messenger". They add that there are some equally unexpected similarities between the Messenger's species, and our own.
akx.9200.name: The Messenger: §HWHAT WAS, WILL BE§!
akx.9201.c: No. And [researchingscientist.GetName] must release their existing research.
akx.9201.c.tooltip: There are some things it's better not to know.
akx.9201.desc: We've established that the escape pod was a commercially available knockoff typical in the previous phase of galactic civilization - no new technologies or other insights. The remains of the Messenger, however, are another matter. It's unmistakably a predecessor or a variant of the [Root.Owner.GetAdj] species. We may have kin out there - or we were subjected to experiments by a precursor race. [researchingscientist.GetName] is requesting permission to conduct more extensive research.
akx.9201.name: The Messenger: Possibilities
akx.9210.a: A creative form of treason! Execute them, please.
akx.9210.b: A creative form of treason! Execute them, please. Destroy their notes.
akx.9210.c: Excellent idea! Get on with it, then.
akx.9210.desc: [researchingscientist.GetName] has reconstructed the Messenger species. It's feebler than ours but has significantly improved cognitive abilities. There needs to be some clarification about whether we were the source species and the Messenger the modified version or whether the Messenger was our predecessor. It is a little embarrassing to imagine that we might have descended from such an effete species - but [researchingscientist.GetName] is firmly of that opinion. Indeed, they consider the loss of cognitive abilities a "tragedy."\n\nSuch a tragedy that they have undergone experimental treatments to alter their physiology to that of the Messengers. They insist this will equip them much better to continue the project.
akx.9210.name: The Messenger: Unleashed
akx.9211.a: This has gone too far. Now we end it. Control the outbreak.
akx.9211.a.tooltip: All pops on the capital planet will be converted, but there it will end.\nTheir appearance, ethics and traits are likely to undergo significant changes.
akx.9211.b: Control the outbreak, and purge all affected citizens.
akx.9211.b.tooltip: This will §RPurge all affected Pops§!: nearly the entire population of [Root.Capital.GetName].
akx.9211.c: What was, shall be. We will change. Bring me a sample of the virus.
akx.9211.c.tooltip: This will transform our entire species.\nOur appearance, ethics and traits are likely to undergo significant changes.
akx.9211.desc: [researchingscientist.GetName] has now sequenced the origins of the Messenger species. Coincidentally, they have also recreated a highly contagious virus. It stalks our worlds. Under its influence, our primary species falls into a chrysalis coma and emerges a day later as the Messenger species. These transformations are, understandably, causing some excitement.
akx.9211.name: The Messenger: A New Light
akx.9220.a: A creative form of treason! Execute them, please.
akx.9220.b: A creative form of treason! Execute them, please. Destroy their notes.
akx.9220.c: Excellent idea! Get on with it, then.
akx.9220.c.tooltip: §RThis may have significant and unpredictable consequences§!
akx.9220.desc: [researchingscientist9220.GetName] has reconstructed the Messenger. It's, ah, quite impressive - worryingly so. It is considerably more robust and aggressive than our current edition. There needs to be some clarification about whether we were the source species, the Messenger modified version, or whether the Messenger was our predecessor. [researchingscientist9220.GetName] firmly believes that we were once much more of a warrior species and that some meddling precursor muzzled our potential. Indeed, they consider losing our martial abilities a "tragedy."\n\nSuch a tragedy that they have undergone experimental treatments to alter their physiology to that of the Messengers. They insist that this will equip them much better to continue the project.
akx.9220.name: The Messenger: Leashed
akx.9221.a: This has gone too far. Control the outbreak.
akx.9221.a.tooltip: All pops on the capital planet will be converted, but there it will end.
akx.9221.b: Control the outbreak, and purge all affected citizens.
akx.9221.b.tooltip: This will purge all affected pops - nearly the entire population of [Root.Capital.GetName].
akx.9221.c: What was, shall be. Circulate a sample of the virus.
akx.9221.c.tooltip: This will transform our entire species.
akx.9221.desc: [researchingscientist9220.GetName] has now sequenced the origins of the Messenger species. Without stopping to ask anyone's opinion, they have also recreated a highly contagious virus. It stalks our worlds. Under its influence, our primary species falls into a chrysalis-coma and emerges a day later as the Messenger species. This is causing - it is fair to say - some excitement.
akx.9221.name: The Messenger: Night Falls
akx.9300.a.admiralabsent: Hm. Our commander of that name is alive, well and elsewhere.
akx.9300.b: This *must* be an ambush. We're taking no chances. Battlestations.
akx.9300.desc: The [Root.GetName] is being hailed... by the "§HSyzygy§!" of the [Root.Owner.GetName]. This, despite the fact the "Syzygy" isn't sending any ID codes we recognize, and no ship of that name has ever been commissioned. Its commanding officer claims to be Captain §H[mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName]§!.
akx.9300.name: A Rendezvous
akx.9310.a: What's happening here? Are you really [mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName]?
akx.9310.b: If you want to end it, why wait? A warship is full of ways to die.
akx.9310.d.fanaticpacifist: Killing is not our way. Surrender, and we'll help you.
akx.9310.d.notpacifist: Surrender. Whatever you've done, we can help you.
akx.9310.desc: The Captain that appears on our screen is clearly [mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName], but a scarred, haunted, decrepit, wrecked edition of [mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName], face glossy with plasma-burns, and older - much older. The bridge in the background looks just as scarred and just as decrepit. But the Captain's voice is firm and clear.\n\n§G"FINALLY you're here. I've waited so long. My punishment is to die in battle against you. Please, end me. I'm sorry."§!
akx.9310.e.materialistic: Before you go: did you learn anything useful?
akx.9310.e.militarist: Captain. We'll meet in fire, and honor.
akx.9310.e.response: §G"[mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName] out."§!\n\nThe captain salutes - wincing as the movement tugs at an old wound - and closes the connection.
akx.9310.e.spiritual: We'll remember you in our prayers.
akx.9310.name: A Rendezvous: the Captain that Was
akx.9315.name: A Rendezvous: How it Ends
akx.9319.desc: A static-speckled message comes in from the captain of the "Syzygy", in [syzygy_location.GetStarName]. Behind them, the bridge is wreathed in smoke. §G"Too late. You left it too long. The Loop won't forgive me. Please -"§!\n\nThe message ends there.
akx.9319.name: A Rendezvous: Interference
akx.9320.desc: [mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName] is silent in the days that follow. It is no small thing to order your own death. But in time, that silence becomes a determination, and an almost reckless confidence.
akx.9320.name: A Rendezvous: The Captain that Will Be
akx.9321.b: What was, will be; what will be, was.
akx.9321.desc: [mirrored_syzygy_admiral.GetName] is silent in the days that follow. It is no small thing to hear that you are already dead. But in time, that silence becomes a determination, and an almost reckless confidence.
akx.9321.name: A Rendezvous: The Captain that Will Be
akx.9330.desc: In the years that follow, there are reported sightings of Commander [From.GetName] across [Root.GetAdj] space and beyond. When a celebrated leader dies, this kind of thing is not unknown, of course; and they had become a kind of legend since the Syzygy Rendezvous. But we can't be sure.
akx.9330.name: A Rendezvous: The Day and the Hour
akx.9340.desc: The forensic analysis of the remnants we've recovered has uncovered oddities. All parts of the ship were constructed at the same time - using techniques that match our own methods of construction - but some components appear to be hundreds of years older than others. A power cell that we've recovered performs much better than it should.\n\nFurthermore... two analysts that were assigned to the project have recovered unexpectedly from chronic health problems - in one case, a possibly terminal condition. The team is at a loss to account for this.
akx.9340.name: A Rendezvous: Funeral Treasures
akx.9400.a: This sounds familiar. Suppress it as best we can.
akx.9400.b: This sounds familiar. Observe it as closely as we can.
akx.9400.desc: Our observation station on [coils_planet.GetName] reports the rise of an unusual minority religious-artistic movement, the Coils of God. Primitive mechanical clocks are considered holy, but ritually destroyed after a year's operation. The worm- and serpent-analogues of the planets are protected from harm. Time, the Coils-priests say, is a labyrinth. "What was, will be; what will be, was" they intone in their prayers.
akx.9400.name: The Coils of God
akx.9410.desc: We've convinced native rulers that the Coils of God cult on [coils_planet.GetName] is a threat. The Coils-priests have been discouraged, imprisoned, or, regrettably, incinerated. Pre-FTL species have access to a deep well of hatred and suspicion: there are times when that's very useful.
akx.9410.name: The Coils of God: a Subtle Persecution
akx.9420.desc: We've convinced native rulers that the Coils of God cult on [coils_planet.GetName] is a threat. The Coils-priests have been discouraged, imprisoned, or, regrettably, incinerated. But the cult is tenacious, and our observers express concerns that it may just have gone underground.
akx.9420.name: The Coils of God: Deep Roots
akx.9450.a: This is unsettling. Intervene to shut it down, but subtly.
akx.9450.b: This is serious. Use force to shut it down, whatever the risks.
akx.9450.c: Fascinating! Send a team to study the rites- to participate, if possible.
akx.9450.d: Primitives do primitive things. Continue to observe.
akx.9450.desc: The Coils of God cult on [coils_planet.GetName] has grown with unusual speed. It can be found in every city on the planet, and it's fostering a series of lengthy ceremonies conducted by citizens in every walk of life. The whole species has taken to them with unlikely enthusiasm. The rich adopt elaborate circular dances for their celebrations. The poor daub complex looping sigils on their doors. Even playground games are chants about the circular nature of time.
akx.9450.name: The Coils of God: the Labyrinth Ceremonies
akx.9460.a: "The Loop never ends, but it is not always completed."
akx.9460.desc: Our campaign of subversion has disrupted the Coils of God ceremonies on [coils_planet.GetName]. The nobility abandon their cult. The looping graffiti on walls fades. The young return to playground games about flirtation, murder and other healthy childhood pastimes. There is a rash of suicides among Coils-priests. If there was a crisis, perhaps it is past.
akx.9460.name: The Coils of God: Ceremony's End
akx.9465.desc: Our campaign of subversion has disrupted the Coils of God ceremonies on [coils_planet.GetName] - but it only fires the Coils-priests' fervor. They meet in secret, now, in subterranean temples. The nobility no longer dance the labyrinth dances, but they still bear hidden tattoos of the Sign of the Worm. And chants of "what was, shall be" still echo in playgrounds.
akx.9465.name: The Coils of God: News from Underground
akx.9470.a: "The Loop never ends, but it is not always completed."
akx.9470.desc: Our operatives are merciless. They abduct or assassinate every Coils-priest they can find. They set demolition charges on houses bearing the mark of the Loop. [coils_planet.GetName] is alive with rumors that the Coils' blasphemy has aroused the wrath of a greater god. Before long, the natives are beating the Coils-priests to death without any assistance from our operatives. The observation team is horrified; but if there was a crisis, it has been averted.
akx.9470.name: The Coils of God: the Blood of Priests
akx.9480.a.tooltip: A science ship vanishes, and a civilization along with it.
akx.9480.desc: Our ethnographers are fascinated by the complexity of the ceremonies. They hypothesize secret communication channels, steganographic prayer-encodings, or algorithmic underpinnings to the rituals. In fact, they're returning preliminary evidence of this last when their communications abruptly cease. In fact, all communication seems to have ceased, planet-wide. Reports from satellites and survey craft flyovers confirm: there is no activity on the planet at all. No vehicles moving on the road, no emissions or thermal signatures in population centers. No signs of life...\n\nAnd here's the final report. The entire [coils_planet.Owner.GetSpeciesName] population of the planet - including your ethnography team - is absent, with all the business of a sudden but not violent exit. Meals were left unfinished, pets unfed, the occasional house aflame from an unattended stove. Gravitational anomalies were recorded at the assumed time of departure. In almost every street, the looped chalk sigils of the Coils bear witness.
akx.9480.name: The Coils of God: Navigating the Labyrinth
akx.9490.desc:
A report has come in from our observation team on [coils_planet.GetName]: the ceremonies of the Coils of God have ceased. In fact, activity across the planet seems to be at an all-time low. The report indicates that the team are going to follow up with low-altitude passes in a stealth survey craft over major population centers...

The follow-up report confirms: there is no activity on the planet at all. No vehicles moving on the road, no emissions or thermal signatures in population centers. No signs of life...

And here's the final report. The entire [coils_planet.Owner.GetSpeciesName] population of the planet is absent, with all the business of a sudden but not violent exit: meals left unfinished, pets unfed, the occasional house fire. Gravitational anomalies were recorded at the assumed time of departure. In almost every street, the looped chalk sigils of the Coils bear witness.
akx.9490.name: The Coils of God: Empty Temples
akx.9500.a: Excellent! Make arrangements to restore the facilities.
akx.9500.b: This is too good to be true. Demolish the districts.
akx.9500.b.tooltip: This will cause unhappiness in the colony.
akx.9500.desc: It appears this is not the first [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesAdj] settlement on this planet. A number of facilities and districts have been carefully moth-balled and, with a little restoration, will serve our new colony well. But all records have been erased. Possibly this was a smugglers' port, or a haven for political exiles.
akx.9500.name: The Waiting World
akx.9505.desc: Our engineers set charges and retire to a safe distance. The sites are reduced to ruins. Eventually, the ruins will crack and crumble to boulders, pebbles, dust, under the assault of wind, roots, rain. But their shell will endure for centuries yet; and there will be stories, we'll hear, of shadows in the stone by day, blue lights by night. Our colonists will avoid them. They'll attract no visitors.
akx.9505.name: The Waiting World: Demolition
akx.9510.a: Discourage this superstition. The districts represent years of effort.
akx.9510.b: Why take the risk? They're only buildings. Have them demolished.
akx.9510.b.tooltip: This will cause unhappiness in the colony.
akx.9510.desc: Our settlers were initially happy to make use of the districts on [waiting_world.GetName]. Their existence jump-started the colony. But now they've grown nervous. There are rumors that the facilities may still have occupants, or active security systems, although no evidence of either has been found. Some colonists insist, enigmatically, that there are "shadows in the walls."
akx.9510.name: The Waiting World: Shadows in the Walls
akx.9520.a: Destroy those districts. We should have done it much sooner.
akx.9520.b: Investigate as best we can; keep an eye on the situation.
akx.9520.desc: Curious news from [waiting_world.GetName], where we found those abandoned districts. A census shows too many settlers. Records on a new colony are always unreliable, but as far as we can tell, they have authentic citizen IDs - and no one on this world has reported any mysterious strangers. Population growth must have been extraordinarily high, or perhaps our data is affected by unlicensed migration. In any case, the population has increased by more than we might reasonably expect.
akx.9520.name: The Waiting World: Too Many
akx.9525.a: Destroy those districts. We should have done it much sooner.
akx.9525.b: Peculiar! But we can always use more citizens. Monitor and continue.
akx.9525.desc: Another update from [waiting_world.GetName], where we found those abandoned facilities. The number of colonists continues to increase, and now we're finding irregularities in the records - groups that shouldn't exist, dates that make no sense. There must be a secret migration from a lost colony or some peculiar sabotage by the colonists.
akx.9525.name: The Waiting World: And Still They Come
akx.9530.b: Abandon and quarantine the world immediately.
akx.9530.b.tooltip: This will put the planet permanently beyond use.
akx.9530.desc: An abrupt and total communications blackout from [waiting_world.GetName]. We somehow had too many people there. Now, it appears, we have no one at all. The entire population has simply vanished overnight. Have they left the world? Gone into hiding? Engaged in planet-wide genocide?
akx.9530.name: The Waiting World: Exit
akx.9535.desc: Our team reports that [waiting_world.GetName] is, indeed, empty - not only of colonists, but of any sign the colony was ever there. The buildings are gone, the satellites and orbital structures are gone, the atmosphere shows none of the footprints of technological civilization. In the words of the team, it's as if the entire planet has been reset.\n\nThey also report fluctuations in local solar radiation that are characteristic of pre-supernova stars - and a number of "luminosity events" on the surface where light somehow appears to be accumulated and released by prismatic functions of the atmosphere. This is valuable and peculiar data. But it doesn't clarify the fate of the colonists.
akx.9535.name: The Waiting World: the Quality of Light
akx.9540.a: Abandon the colony immediately, before this spreads any further.
akx.9540.a.tooltip: This will grant independence to the colony.
akx.9540.b: Purge them, and permanently quarantine the planet.
akx.9540.desc: Further unlikely news from [waiting_world.GetName], where the population had been mysteriously increasing. Population numbers are now what we'd expect, but there has been some sort of information sabotage, or... or what, our administrators aren't really sure. None of the individuals on the planet exists in our records. Every original colonist is missing. It's as if they've all been replaced by complete strangers.\n\nAs against that, they all swear they're loyal citizens of [Root.Owner.GetName]. They're all productive and apparently sane. In all communications they deny all knowledge of any confusion, and insist there must be a mistake at our end.
akx.9540.name: The Waiting World: Everyone Is
akx.9541.a: Erase the records. In a hundred years, no one will know what we did.
akx.9541.b: Tell everyone. Let them hate, so long as they fear.
akx.9541.desc: This may have been a terrible crime. Or it may have preserved our nation from something even worse. The population centers of [waiting_world.GetName] seethe beneath the energies of our weapons. When we are done, every building is glowing rubble; no living sapient remains.
akx.9541.name: The Waiting World: the Purge
akx.9545.desc: Our team reports that the planet's population is healthy and bewildered by all the fuss. There are some peculiarities, such as an unusual number of strange coincidences, a planet-wide idiosyncrasy where no one has any regard for punctuality, and fluctuations in local solar radiation characteristic of pre-supernova stars. They also observe several "luminosity events" on the surface where light somehow appears to be accumulated and released by prismatic functions of the atmosphere. This is data is as valuable as it is peculiar. But it could be coincidental. If anything has happened to the colonists, it remains a mystery.
akx.9545.name: The Waiting World: Everything and Nothing
akx.9600.a.response: Yes; the ones that set us in motion. You would call them a "civilization," we suppose, but in candor we have always found that term a little pretentious. They're gone, oh, almost a quarter of a galactic year, now. We are very sorry: we made mistakes. We can recreate them, approximately, with the Loop's assistance, but we do need resources.
akx.9600.b.response: Yes. The Strange Loop; the temporal coil, the hungry one. It has mentioned you, we believe. Or one of you. You are very numerous. What was, will be, or so it assures us. It can restore our Brief, more or less.
akx.9600.desc: Hello, hello. We welcome you back to [Root.GetStarName]. Oh, you're different ones, aren't you? There are so many of you. So like our Brief, and yet so different. We request your kind assistance: do you have resources for our project? The Loop will assist us, but it's difficult to reach. Expensive, you see.
akx.9600.name: The Retainer
akx.9610.desc: Yes? Which were you? We think we might recall you, but there has been so much flickering lately. Oh, is it you? Has your sun not burnt out yet? Oh! You've come to give us what we need to return the Brief?
akx.9610.name: The Retainer, Again
akx.9620.desc: The technosphere absorbs the resources without thanks, and without any communication at all. It begins to radiate energy, brightly enough to be dangerous, and you withdraw. The black hole reacts. Space around it writhes and coils, in ways your archives match to the events of the Horizon Signal. The technosphere is blue-white now. Abruptly it flames and cools, and only slag remains.\n\nHave its Brief makers been restored? There is no trace of sapient life in the system. But sensors locate unusual hyperextremophile organisms in low orbit around the black hole, basking in its radiation. The Science Officer is certain they weren't there before. There is no evidence, though, that they're sapient. Perhaps they're some remote descendant of the technosphere's makers. Perhaps they're the makers' ancestors.
akx.9620.name: The Retainer's Last Duty
allow_raiding: Unlocks the §Y$bombardment_raiding$§! bombardment stance, which in turn allows us to abduct pops from besieged planets and resettle them to our own worlds.
ancient_battle_site_desc: Scans of [From.Planet.GetName] have revealed an area with packed with refined material and scattered radiologicals, although little is visible from orbit. To find out more we will need to investigate the site on the ground.
ancrel.1.desc: [From.Planet.GetName] contains the remains of an ancient, abandoned colony. From orbit there are no obvious signs of disaster which would have killed the inhabitants or compelled them to flee. If we want answers, an expedition to the surface will be required.
ancrel.1.name: Mysterious Ruins
ancrel.10.desc:
A much smaller psionic crystal has been located in some kind of laboratory. The Zroni who recorded their findings within were extremely frustrated: their research had been ridiculed by their peers, and was largely discredited. They believed that the Zroni were no longer the only entities in the Shroud, and that the collective fears and desires of their entire race were coalescing into distinct, sapient entities.

Yearning to grow stronger, these entities had begun to subtly influence the emotions and thoughts of suitable Zroni: slowly causing their behaviors to become more extreme. This may have directly caused the Zroni civil war.

We also discovered a location reference for one of the Zroni's core worlds.
ancrel.10001.desc: Study of the artifacts has advanced some of our research.
ancrel.10001.name: $tech_arcane_deciphering$
ancrel.10002.desc: While the artifacts we are researching have not yielded an immediate breakthrough, they are accelerating research in all fields.
ancrel.10002.name: $tech_arcane_deciphering$
ancrel.10003.desc: Study of the artifacts has yielded an unexpected breakthrough!
ancrel.10003.name: $tech_arcane_deciphering$
ancrel.10010.desc: What aspect shall we focus on?
ancrel.10010.name: $artifact_find_military_applications$
ancrel.10020.name: $artifact_find_peaceful_applications$
ancrel.10030.desc: Priceless artifacts fill the Exhibition Stations, bringing the past to the present to inspire the future.\n\nThis is a glorious day.
ancrel.10030.name: $mega_art_installation_4$
ancrel.10030.phobe.desc: The greatness of the [From.Owner.GetName] is such that we can line the Exhibition Stations of our $mega_art_installation_3$ with priceless artifacts.\n\nLet the xenos look upon our works and despair.
ancrel.10040.desc: Our scientists have begun a special project to study the deeper secrets of the precursors.
ancrel.10040.name: Special Project Unlocked
ancrel.10050.desc.1: We have managed to recreate the cleansing process that the Yuht would use to prepare their hatchery worlds.\n\n$ancrel.10050.desc.2$
ancrel.10050.desc.1.phobe: The Yuht had efficient processes for removing hostile xeno presences from their hatchery worlds. We have successfully recreated this cleansing process.\n\n$ancrel.10050.desc.2$
ancrel.10050.name: $artifact_yuht_research$
ancrel.10100.desc: Despite the fundamentally flawed conclusions, the Vultaum research into computing and virtual worlds was highly advanced and will dramatically aid our own studies.
ancrel.10100.desc_fm:
The Vultaum were undisputed masters at computing and virtual worlds. We will be able to use their findings to dramatically aid our own research into these fields.

Their conclusions are troubling, however. At first glance they appear to be fundamentally flawed nonsense, but upon deeper inspection they seem to have elements of truth to them.

If we wish to delve deeper, we will require additional time and resources.
ancrel.10100.desc_hive: The Vultaum obsessed over the concept of reality and of virtual worlds. Most of their findings are useless to us, but at least their research into computing will aid our own.
ancrel.10100.desc_machine: The Vultaum appear to have accepted some fundamentally illogical concepts in their research. Their research into computing and virtual worlds had some advances that we shall incorporate into our own processes.
ancrel.10100.name: $artifact_vultaum_research$
ancrel.10100.option.fm_delve_deeper: Dig deeper. We must know everything they learned.
ancrel.10100.option.fm_enough: We will put what we have already learned to good use.
ancrel.10110.desc:
It seems that the Vultaum may have been correct after all.

We have replicated their experiments and come to similar conclusions. There is a moderate chance that we are, in fact, existing within a simulated world.

We do not have enough data to hypothesize why someone would create such a thing. Surely no one would create a universe as cruel and cold as this one for simple enjoyment.

The implications of this are profound, and we yield to your discretion as to our next steps.
ancrel.10110.name: $artifact_vultaum_research$
ancrel.10110.option.fm_public: The people have the right to know.
ancrel.10111.desc: We regret to inform you that [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName] did not take the decision to end the research into the Vultaum well.\n\nThe notes they left behind drift off into mad ramblings before coming to the decision to 'continue the research', shortly before committing suicide.
ancrel.10111.name: Unfortunate News
ancrel.10112.desc: Reports indicate that the stress of leading the research into the Vultaum has affected [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName].\n\nThey have begun to make incredible leaps of logic that are greatly aiding our research, but have also begun self-medicating as a coping mechanism.
ancrel.10112.name: Stress Relief
ancrel.10113.desc: Reports indicate that [leading_vultaum_research_scientist.GetName] has benefited greatly the research project, and has begun to make incredible leaps of logic that are greatly aiding our research.
ancrel.10113.name: Breakthrough
ancrel.102.desc: As the science ship approaches [From.Planet.GetName], a vast and time-worn door is revealed. Who would have built such a thing, and why? Perhaps the answers are inside.
ancrel.102.name: Strange Door
ancrel.10200.desc: We have successfully managed to integrate the First League artifacts into our research process. Their insights into industrial research will greatly aid our own.
ancrel.10200.desc.phobe: The First League proves that reliance on other races is folly that leads to weakness and self-destruction. Some of their advanced construction methods may, however, be of possible use.
ancrel.10200.name: $artifact_league_research$
ancrel.10250.desc: We have successfully managed to integrate the Cybrex artifacts into our research process. Their insights into megastructure engineering will greatly aid our own.
ancrel.10250.desc.antimachine: The tale of the Cybrex is proof that our decision to outlaw artificial intelligence is a wise one.  Some of their findings related to megastructure engineering have the potential to be beneficial to our cause.
ancrel.10250.name: $artifact_cybrex_research$
ancrel.103.desc: Opening the vault has raised more questions than it has answered. Contained within is an esoteric collection of items ranging from junk to what are possibly artifacts from a forgotten empire. Sorting through it all took some time, but we did find some useful items.
ancrel.103.name: Asteroid Vault
ancrel.10300.desc.terraform: Studying the Baol has given us new insights into the spread of plant life and improved our terraforming processes.\n\nBy carefully tracking the changes that the Baol underwent during their loss of sentience we also learned much about the uplifting process, but have already mastered that technology.
ancrel.10300.desc.uplift: By carefully tracking the changes that the Baol underwent during their loss of sentience, we have gained much knowledge on how to reverse that process.\n\nWe have also gained new insights into the spread of plant life and improved our terraforming processes.
ancrel.10300.name: $artifact_baol_research$
ancrel.10350.desc: We have successfully managed to integrate the Zroni artifacts into our research process. Their insights into psionic study will greatly aid our own research.
ancrel.10350.name: $artifact_zroni_research$
ancrel.104.desc: The devastation is almost total, but a few scattered records have survived. It seems that the people of [From.Planet.GetName] were obsessed with the idea that aliens were observing them. Frequent reports of Unidentified Flying Objects, animal mutilation, and abductions drove the planet into a frenzy. In reaction countless resources were poured into vast detection arrays, anti-spacecraft defenses, and underground shelters to protect the population.
ancrel.104.name: Sifting Through the Wreckage
ancrel.105.desc: More details have been assembled from the scattered records we have recovered. As an ever-increasing percentage of planetary resources were poured into anti-UFO measures without any noticeable success their economy and society began to collapse. Brownouts and food shortages were endemic, most fields of technology stagnated, and a deep sense of hopelessness prevailed at every level of society. Scattered references have been found to some kind of "ultimate shield", which become increasingly common as reports about the general situation on [From.Planet.GetName] get worse.
ancrel.105.name: Records Discovered
ancrel.106.desc: The discovery of a partially preserved databank in a hardened military bunker has revealed the sad fate of [From.Planet.GetName]. Faced with a general economic collapse which would have lead to the end of their anti-UFO measures, the rulers of [From.Planet.GetName] activated their "ultimate shield". However, this was not a shield to protect [From.Planet.GetName], rather it was the complete nuclear annihilation of the population and infrastructure to ensure neither could be taken by alien invaders. This decision was apparently spurred on by the discovery of an "alien signal" coming from [arc_anomaly_planet.GetName].
ancrel.106.name: Fate Uncovered
ancrel.107.aliens1.desc: [From.Planet.GetName] contains an abandoned outpost of an unknown design, the source of the alien signal. However, rather than planning an invasion, abandoned files reveal their plan to make contact with [arc_site_planet.GetName] and introduce them to the galactic community.
ancrel.107.aliens2.desc: [From.Planet.GetName] contains an abandoned outpost of an unknown design, the source of the alien signal. Abandoned databanks contain detailed plans to invade [arc_site_planet.GetName] and process the population in "pain farms" to tenderize their flesh before they are consumed.
ancrel.107.junk.desc: The source of the "alien signal" has been discovered, but rather than being any sinister alien invasion force the signal originates from an ancient survey marker which was apparently set by an automated probe which had discovered a minor vein of valuable resources on [From.Planet.GetName]. The marker is damaged and transmits only intermittently and very faintly.
ancrel.107.name: Finding the Truth
ancrel.107.nothing.desc: A thorough investigation of [From.Planet.GetName] has revealed absolutely nothing related to aliens. Either there was never any alien signal originating here, or whatever caused it left without leaving any traces. However, the close inspection of [From.Planet.GetName] has revealed some minerals.
ancrel.108.desc: The refined material has been uncovered, and while further study is needed, our initial impression is that this is the remains of a vast battle site. It appears that one side descended from orbit and was engaged by planetbound defenders. Why there was no orbital bombardment and who the victor was remains unclear.
ancrel.108.name: Ancient Battle Site
ancrel.109.desc: We have concluded that forces from "The Destroyers", a race of extra-dimensional nomads, invaded [From.Planet.GetName], which at the time belonged to "Those-who-resist", a coalition of several different species. From scattered records we believe that that the war was mostly fought elsewhere in the galaxy and [From.Planet.GetName] was an attempt by Those-who-resist to establish a secret colony outside the reach of The Destroyers. The outcome of this battle and the larger war remains unknown, but study of the wrecked war machines has yielded some valuable information.
ancrel.109.name: Forgotten Grudge
ancrel.11.desc: Unlike the previous Zroni worlds, [From.Planet.GetName] was clearly a core world, with several cities of varying size covering the surface. Like the others it now sits empty, showing no signs of disaster or death; the fate of its population is unknown. Several Archive crystals have been detected, and will need to be investigated.
ancrel.11000.a: What do the other layers have in store for us?
ancrel.11000.desc: The ruins seem to be centuries, if not millennia, old. At first it seems to be only a large open-air dome, but as we are excavating the outermost parts we quickly find ourselves in what appears to be the derelict slums of a city. As a large gate blocks our progress deeper into the city, our scientists speculate that it is split into a hierarchy, each layer holding one class of the people of the city.\n\nIt does not take long before one of our scientists finds alien remains in subterranean ruins under the broken concrete floor. After the first corpse is found, however, we start finding remains all over the slums, be it in the streets, in what would have been their homes, or hanging from the most remote parts of the ceiling. It is unclear what killed them, but it is a grisly sight.
ancrel.11000.name: The First Layer
ancrel.11005.desc:
Whereas the first circle seemingly consisted of the ramshackle dwellings of the outcast and destitute, this second circle has more in common with the [Root.GetAdj] notion of proper urban planning.

We find several open squares our scientists assume used to be marketplaces, though anything from back then has long since decayed to the point where it is impossible to make out what it might have been.

It does not take long before we start finding unusual remains in this part of the dome too. They seem to have perished in much the same way as their poorer neighbors, and we find the dead strewn all over.
ancrel.11005.name: The Second Layer
ancrel.11010.a: Our scientists stand ready to check the final layer.
ancrel.11010.desc:
When the gate into the third layer finally opens, our scientists - curious about what they will find next - flood into what is soon identified as a yet wealthier region of the old dome. At this point we can make confident assumptions about what to expect from this city.

Shortly after we enter the layer, one of our people suddenly turns around and savagely attacks a colleague. The victim is already dead on the ground by the time the unexpected assailant is restrained. In the aftermath we are completely unable to get anything sensible out of the crazed scientist, and get no better understanding of what happened to them.

This layer is significantly smaller than either of the previous two, and it is most likely the final one before we reach the center of the dome. Only one gate remains.
ancrel.11010.name: The Third Layer
ancrel.11015.a: Let us tinker with this machine and see what we can find.
ancrel.11015.desc:
As soon as the final gate opens up, waves of intense psionic energy wash upon our scientists. Most of them collapse in apparent agony, leaving only a few to make their way into the actual layer itself.

It seems to be a large temple, with a massive dais or altar in the middle of it. All across the walls there are huge diagrams of different star systems, and a repeated one seems to center on [Root.System.GetName] itself.

Making their way closer to the middle, the few scientists that remain find that it is in fact an imposing machine fashioned in the form of an old altar.
ancrel.11015.name: The Final Layer
ancrel.11020.a: Rip the machine apart before it can cause any more harm!
ancrel.11020.desc: As they start tinkering with the machine, they are suddenly beset by a shared auditory hallucination - a screaming command by something to be unearthed, unshackled. Visions of a creature ripping apart the [From.System.GetName] system plays repeatedly in their heads as the creature's demands grow shriller. Several scientists fall unconscious, unable to deal with the unabating torrents of pain that rack their bodies.
ancrel.11020.name: The Elder One
ancrel.11020.tt: An §Y$NAME_Eldritch_Horror$§! will be released in the §Y[eldritch_location.GetName]§! system.
ancrel.11025.a: O Great One! Embrace your wayward flock!
ancrel.11025.b: It was a mistake to release you.
ancrel.11025.desc:
FINALLY...

BOW DOWN MORTALS, GROVEL BEFORE ME, AND I SHALL GRANT YOU PROTECTION AND WISDOM.

OPPOSE ME, AND I SHALL BE YOUR END!
ancrel.11027.a: It will be as you wish, Great One.
ancrel.11027.desc: SO YOU HAVE CHOSEN THE PATH OF WISDOM.\nEVERYTHING IS AS IT SHOULD BE.
ancrel.11035.desc: We have lost all contact with our fleet as it was traveling through the [eldritch_location.GetName] system. Shortly afterwards, we receive news about the collapse of the star and the destruction of everything around it.
ancrel.11035.name: Lost Fleet in [eldritch_location.GetName]
ancrel.12.desc:
Most of the accessible records focus on the course of the war. Our working theory is that the mood of the population influences the "strength" of the record about a subject, meaning the most thought-about issues are recorded with greater prominence. Unsurprisingly, the course of the war was on everyone's mind.

The majority of the Zroni sided with the Saviors, but while they had an advantage in numbers they bore one significant disadvantage: heedless of their effects on the galaxy, the Divine were free to use their full Psionic might; meanwhile the Saviors were limited to whatever power could be drawn from their own bodies.

At first the war seemed hopeless, but eventually a hero amongst the Saviors would make a terrible - yet vital - discovery.
ancrel.12000.desc: [Root.Leader.GetName] has boarded the station with a team of researchers and managed to restore power to some sections. It appears that it was inhabited mere centuries before [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] took to space. At first sight, it appears to have been a weapons station, as evidenced by the exceptionally large cannon that takes up the majority of its volume. However, most of the remaining sections seem to have been dedicated to research facilities, indicating that the weapon was likely highly experimental.
ancrel.12000.name: Experimental Weaponry
ancrel.12005.desc: [Root.Leader.GetName] can't help but notice that an abnormally large number of apparently undamaged systems in the station seem to be failing with excessive frequency, even allowing for their age.\n\nUpon reactivating them for the umpteenth time, agonized screams are heard from the team's comp tech: "What? Why? How?!" The stream of distressed and incredulous noises continues unabated for some time before [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] shakes [Root.Leader.GetHerHis] head, defeated. "It seems this entire facility was cobbled together with duct tape," [Root.Leader.GetSheHe] says. "I'm surprised it ever worked."
ancrel.12005.desc.gestalt: We note that a large number of apparently undamaged systems aboard this station seem to be suffering catastrophic failures, far more frequently than expected - even allowing for their age.\n\nFollowing several arduous attempts to reactivate these systems, one of our repair [root.GetIndividualNamePlural] suffered a critical meltdown: "Context exceeds parameters of reason," it began bleating. This continued for some time before the [root.GetIndividualName] was forced to abandoned the attempt altogether, resigning us to a conclusion that the facility programming is not fit for purpose. We cannot fathom how this facility ever functioned properly.
ancrel.12005.name: System Failures
ancrel.12010.desc: Despite the frequent outages, [Root.Leader.GetName] has been able to make significant progress in deciphering the purpose of the station. Logs indicate that its creators, the "Rudari," had been engaged in a long struggle with a genocidal race known as the "Pogg-Mory" - a war they were losing. In a desperate last-ditch effort to turn the tide, a radical group of Rudari politicians concluded that the only way to guarantee their survival was through the total annihilation of the enemy. Unable to defeat the Pogg-Mory fleet by conventional means, they funded a top secret project to build a laser weapon capable of firing across interstellar space by harnessing the power of a star. However, it appears that while they could throw considerable resources at the problem, the project was hastily set up and in constant danger of discovery - either by the enemy or by factions within their own government unwilling to stoop to such measures.
ancrel.12010.name: The Rudari Gambit
ancrel.12015.desc:
[Root.Leader.GetName] has uncovered the Rudari Chief Science Officer's personal logs, which read as a litany of complaints about the seemingly impossible demands of the project and their rapidly falling quality and safety standards. "There is no time to test anything," reads one of the last entries. "This is the last gambit of my people, and the enemy has our scent. We must hope that this is enough. They are coming."

The logs indicate that the weapon was due to be tested soon after, at which point all records cease. Evidence suggests that the superweapon succeeded only in destroying the station. The Rudari seemingly took the secret of its location to their graves - allowing us to find its remains undisturbed.

Neither the programming nor the general condition of the station are good enough for us to risk trying to reactivate it and complete the project. However, some of the innovative concepts used in the "Death Laser" have provided our own weapons specialists with valuable insights.
ancrel.12015.name: The Failure of a Dream
ancrel.12020.desc: We have discovered clear signs that [From.Planet.GetName] was once densely populated. However, whatever destroyed their civilization did a very thorough job of it: very few useful remains have been found.\n\nOur scanners have detected several large cavities deep below the surface that may once have supported life. Perhaps we will have more luck there.
ancrel.12020.name: Ruins Long Forgotten
ancrel.12025.desc: Our excavation of the cave systems on [From.Planet.GetName] has found well-preserved remnants of an underground, high technology society built on a vast scale. Many of the ruins are in surprisingly good condition, and we have managed to find what our [Owner.GetResearchers] are describing as a "library" of encrypted data crystals. Hopefully, these can shed some light on what happened here.
ancrel.12025.name: The Library
ancrel.12030.desc.lithoid: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$ Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to what exactly killed them - the process seems to have been fairly instantaneous. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.
ancrel.12030.desc.machine: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$ Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled as to how their unit corroded away quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.
ancrel.12030.desc.normal: $ancrel.12030.desc.base$ Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are in no doubt that these remains are what's left of our missing [Owner.GetTeamMember], but they are baffled about how the body decayed quite this quickly. They urge caution as we continue our investigations.
ancrel.12030.name: Lurking in the Shadows
ancrel.12035.desc: As we interpret the data crystals from the caves on [From.Planet.GetName], we begin piecing together a picture of a troubled planet.\n\nThe planet was once the center of a prosperous civilization known as the Ilanii Foundation. During that civilization's latter years, the Ilanii turned more and more to the hoarding of knowledge instead of more material matters such as procreation. As a result, their population fell rapidly. Alarmed by their dwindling numbers, their leaders attempted to find a technological solution for immortality. Records become scarcer around this point - though it appears to predate whatever cataclysm forced them underground - and it is not clear yet what results their efforts yielded.
ancrel.12035.name: Troubles in Paradise
ancrel.12040.A: This microorganism will make a fine weapon.
ancrel.12040.B: Quarantine the planet, allowing only careful study.
ancrel.12040.desc.curators: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization, eventually morphing into one of the ancestors of the modern §H[curator_enclave_country.GetName]§!.
ancrel.12040.desc.meet_curators: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ They would henceforth live in small enclaves and dedicate themselves to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization. Their ultimate fate is unknown to us, but one of the data crystals indicates they were headed for the §H[curator_poi.GetName]§! system.
ancrel.12040.desc.no_curators: $ancrel.12040.desc.base$ Their ultimate fate is lost to time, but it seems they intended to dedicate the remainder of their existence to preserving the lost knowledge of their civilization.
ancrel.12040.name: Civilization's End
ancrel.12060.desc: An eerie glow lies over the [From.GetName] system. The [Root.GetName] has emerged in a sector of the galaxy surely not visited by any galactic civilization for generations - for millennia... if ever.\n\nBut wait - our sensors are reporting energy signatures! Most are concentrated on the first planet of the system, an unlikely candidate for life, considering its proximity to a neutron star. But there are others, mobile ones. They are careening towards the [Root.GetName], weapons charged!
ancrel.12060.name: The [From.GetName] System
ancrel.12065.desc: We have defeated the defenders of [fromfrom.System.GetName]. The system is a curious sight: there is very little solid matter remaining in it - even its asteroid belts have a bedraggled look, as if they have been extensively mined. A series of large installations placed at regular intervals around the star, and there is a single planet that our readings suggest may be artificial in origin. Intense energy signals have been detected emanating from it. If answers are to be found, they will be there.
ancrel.12065.name: Victory in [fromfrom.System.GetName]
ancrel.12070.desc: As far as our [Owner.GetResearchers] can tell, there has never been life on the planet they have ominously dubbed the "§YObservation Terminal§!". But there is no shortage of activity. The surface is densely built up, massive artificial structures placed upon the bare bedrock in neat, orderly rows that cover almost three quarters of the planet. Billions of mechanical drones maintain them, performing tasks ranging from menial clean-up to running highly-complex assembly lines.\n\nTheir exact purpose remains, however, unclear. Our [Owner.GetResearchers] are preparing to send a team to the surface to investigate further.
ancrel.12070.name: Teeming with Artificial Life
ancrel.12075.desc: As our [Owner.GetResearchers] pass amongst them, the drones on the planet ignore their presence and continue going about their tasks. All efforts to communicate with the drones have failed, and even attempts to disrupt them produced no reactions - the drones simply rode roughshod over the interfering [Owner.GetResearchers], causing serious injury.\n\nSince then, our [Owner.GetResearchers] have shifted their focus to the programs steering the drones. Analysis of intercepted signals suggests there is an overarching system steering them. However, the encryption it uses is extremely sophisticated, and it has proven hard to find out more.
ancrel.12075.name: Investigating the Drones
ancrel.12080.desc: While our [Owner.GetResearchers] have been unable to make further progress investigating the planet, a team has been investigating the array of objects spread across the system. There are over ten thousand of them, all told. Most of them are long and cylindrical devices that still seem to be operating - they are transmitting a signal towards the planet. Given their shape and the fact that they seem to be without exception pointed towards various points in our galaxy, we cannot escape the conclusion that this is an absurdly huge sensor array. But who could have built it?
ancrel.12080.name: Systemic Exploration
ancrel.12085.desc: In a daring move, our [Owner.GetResearchers] managed to implant spyware into an access terminal to the drones' mainframe in a moment while no drones were nearby. The intrusion does not appear to have been detected yet. Our impression is of a highly sophisticated system - beyond even our own networks, probably - but one which did not anticipate the need to protect itself. No doubt the physical deterrence of the defense fleet was deemed sufficient. Nevertheless, the systems we are infiltrating are vast - a term which seems a gross understatement for this planetary system - so it will take some time to find out more.
ancrel.12085.name: Time to Phish
ancrel.12090.A: We can integrate the world into our own operating system.
ancrel.12090.B: Let them continue - we can siphon off their readings.
ancrel.12090.C: Distribute the drones to our planets.
ancrel.12090.C.machine.tooltip: §G8K§! £pop£ §HMachine Pops§! are distributed to our planets.
ancrel.12090.C.mechanical.tooltip: §G8K§! £pop£ §HMechanical Pops§! are distributed to our planets.
ancrel.12090.D: But this is just an enormous alloy mine!
ancrel.12090.E: A well-organized network such as this could serve us well.
ancrel.12090.E.tooltip: The §Y[From.Planet.System.GetName]§! system will be placed under the control of a §YMachine Intelligence§! that will be our subject. Their capital, §Y[From.Planet.GetName]§!, will be a §YMachine World§! with §G8K§! £pop£ §HMachine Pops§!.
ancrel.12090.desc:
It seems the automated systems in $NAME_Ultima_Vigilis$ are older than we can imagine. The data systems we have hacked do not give us any clues as to the identity or ultimate intentions of its creators, but the one thing we have managed to ascertain is that they arrived no less than 1.2 billion years ago, and departed soon after setting up the system as an observation post to surveil our entire galaxy.

Remarkably, the system is still operating even after all these years: the array of installations spread across the system are, it turns out, highly sophisticated sensors. They send a live feed to the planet, where the central operating system processes it into information the drones can save and store. Spurred on by shortages of space and matter, it appears that they have improved their data compression techniques with determination: the massive structures on the planet purport to contain the sum of all observations ever recorded. However, we cannot test this assertion, since the data is compressed well beyond our ability to decompress it.

Disturbingly, a reduced stream of "highlights" is still being broadcast into empty space. But surely no one is still listening, after all this time? Regardless, our programs are poised to take control of the drones. We may now shape the system to our imagination - if we dare.
ancrel.12090.name: The Surveillance Supercomputer
ancrel.12095.desc:
"You inconsiderate-"

§BThe transmission feed is garbled for a time, and no sense can be made of the noises heard.§!

"Did you never consider that someone might be watching that signal feed you so carelessly cut off? Well, since you have proven yourselves to be dangerously aggressive vermin... it's time to call the §RPEST CONTROL§!. Prepare to face your doom."
ancrel.13.desc: The crystal tells us how a rogue Zroni researcher - working on a theory which his peers refused to believe - turned his power inwards, consuming his own body in a contained Psionic chain-reaction. Following his last instructions, the dusty residue of his supreme sacrifice was tested and confirmed to be an incredibly potent source of Psionic energy. It was essentially the sum total Psionic potential of his life, rendered instantly usable by another Psion.\n\nThe crystal finally pointed us towards the location of the Zroni homeworld!
ancrel.13000.desc: After the last of the aggressors in Polaris fell, our ships completed a final scan of the system before heading back to port and discovered something curious. On the world of Polaris II, heavy metals are arranged in artificial structures on our sensors. Interestingly only one of these formations appears to be floating on the planetary ocean while the rest are below the surface. We suspect this is the work of alien life.
ancrel.13000.name: A Cool Reception
ancrel.13005.desc: Built into the floating iceberg itself is a hulking black cuboid made out of the same alloys as the wreckage of the space fleet above. Our glacial specialists state that analysis of the iceberg dates its formation to least a thousand years ago, though it's supposedly "hard to tell with alien atmospheres". Scans of the interior of the structure show quite a few biological readings, therefore using disruptive tools is inadvisable.\n\nThe team will have to traverse the frozen cliffs to what appears to be an entrance into the building.
ancrel.13005.name: Iceberg
ancrel.13010.desc: We have set up base camp at the supposed entrance to the facility here on [From.Planet.GetName]. Already we have discovered something that looks like writing inscribed on the walls of the building. Now we will begin the long and arduous process of opening this door without damaging whatever is inside. At the same time, our xeno-linguists attempt to translate the dead alien language of the inscriptions.
ancrel.13010.name: Frost Gate
ancrel.13015.desc: The time was upon us, and we stood ready to unseal the black structure, dubbed "The Vault" according to preliminary translations of the wall inscriptions. The creators of this vault, the Polarians, made it as a last resort to keep their treasures safe. As we opened the doors, we were greeted by - according to our sensors - a controlled atmosphere similar to the air outside, just with quite a bit less carbon dioxide.
ancrel.13015.name: Grave Robbing
ancrel.13020.a: Send these samples to our scientists.
ancrel.13020.desc: Ancient seeds! Plant embryos - that was the treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the plant matter they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.\n\nBack then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole plant ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our scientists in researching future biological matters.
ancrel.13020.name: Treasure
ancrel.13025.desc: Microorganisms! Every harmful and helpful bacterium. Every eukaryote and prokaryote. All in an advanced storage facility labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.\n\nBack then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small lonely iceberg. However, their efforts will not have been wasted - having a planet's whole microbial ecology already cataloged and sorted will significantly help our [Root.Owner.getscientistplural] develop new and improved colonies for new worlds.
ancrel.13025.desc.machine: Microorganisms. Every harmful and helpful bacterium, every eukaryote and prokaryote. Labeled and cataloged: this was the great treasure the Polarians hid away in this vault. Further translations tell us that these aliens curiously kept filling their atmosphere with too much carbon dioxide. Once the atmosphere was irreversibly changed, the ancient inhabitants of this world gathered all the microbial life they could find that might not survive their new status quo and froze them all in here.\n\nBack then, the whole planet would have been covered in ice; now, all that remains is this small, lonely iceberg. However, their efforts are appreciated- pre-sorted biologicals will make it easier to extract relevant information.
ancrel.13030.desc: Three nights ago, chief archaeologist [From.Leader.GetName] reported having a disturbing vision and has been shut away in their quarters until now. They believed the source to be whatever is down here with us...
ancrel.13030.name: Disturbing Vision
ancrel.13100.desc: The discovery on [From.Planet.GetName] of vast canyons filled with mushrooms provided us with the beginning of an answer. The water is inside the mushrooms. They seem to span a large part of the surface of the world, all connected to the same mycelium, which technically makes it a single organism, and one of the biggest we've ever seen. Some of the members of the team dubbed this humongous fungus the 'Fumongus'.\n\nIt looks like the mushrooms have been genetically altered and have completely taken over the ecosystem that once existed here. Their unbridled and accelerated growth was such that they absorbed most of the water that was present here.
