anomaly.4136.a.tooltip: Gives access to the §Y$edict_masters_writings_politics$§! Empire Edict.
anomaly.4136.desc: Having had our linguistics experts hard at work for months, we've finally succeeded in translating the works found on [From.From.From.GetName].The papers are the teachings of an alien scholar only referred to as "Telisa the Teller of Tales." All mentions of her points to her being a famous philosopher and overall expert on society and relations.\n\n$anomaly.4136.base.desc$
anomaly.4136.found.desc: It seems that the text we found on [From.From.From.GetName] is another piece created by "Telisa the Teller of Tales."$anomaly.4136.base.desc$
anomaly.4140.desc: The [Root.GetName]'s crew is reporting that they've found something spectacular on [From.GetName]. On the surface lies traces of an explorative expedition of another civilization. Left behind are some well-preserved documents and artifacts.\n\nThe proposed action by chief Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] is to send the text findings to our homeworld for translation. There is also the possibility to sell them off to a private investor.
anomaly.4140.name: Teachings of Explorers
anomaly.4141.a.tooltip: Gives access to the §Y$edict_masters_writings_philosophy$§! Empire Edict.
anomaly.4141.desc: After many weeks of study, our expert linguists have unearthed the meaning behind the documents found on [From.From.From.GetName]. The documents were philosophical ponderings by a famous scholar, only referred to as "Telisa the Teller of Tales."\n\n$anomaly.4141.base.desc$
anomaly.4141.found.desc: Who would've thought? The texts we found were more teachings from "Telisa the Teller of Tales." This time it's a collection of philosophical ponderings and analysis on larger questions.\n\n$anomaly.4141.base.desc$
anomaly.4150.desc: The surface of [From.GetName] holds something remarkable. Multiple ruins can be found, built using different architectures, yet from the same point in history. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] might have been a trading hub!\n\nSome ruins held stored documents and valuables. If we studied the texts we might be able to translate them and learn more about the people who settled here. Or we could sell them to someone who values old heirlooms.
anomaly.4150.name: Teachings of Traders
anomaly.4151.a.tooltip: Gives access to the §Y$edict_masters_writings_diplomacy$§! Empire Edict.
anomaly.4151.desc: Our most talented linguists have been hard at work in translating the documents we found on [From.From.From.GetName]. The scribe behind these works is referred to as "Telisa the Teller of Tales," and it seems she was highly revered during her time.\n\n$anomaly.4151.base.desc$
anomaly.4151.found.desc: Who would've thought? The texts we found were more teachings from "Telisa the Teller of Tales."\n\n$anomaly.4151.base.desc$
anomaly.4155.a: Let's try and get to it!
anomaly.4155.b: Leave the vault, and its wandering spirits be.
anomaly.4155.desc: [From.GetName] used to hold an advanced civilization. It is now dead silent. Alien beasts roam old battlefields that stretch across the surface.\n\nIn a rocky region there seems to lie a hidden vault beneath the mountains. If we could get rid of the beasts roaming the landscape we could investigate it.
anomaly.4155.name: Beneath the Battlefield
anomaly.4156.b: Only study the vault to avoid risks.
anomaly.4156.desc: With the beasts removed, we could access the vault. Inside it lay a headquarter of sorts, a last refuge for a dying world's leaders.\n\nThe vault is filled with destroyed equipment and decomposed corpses. The only thing of interest being a container, which potentially holds something of importance.
anomaly.4157.a: You are on [HomePlanet.GetName]. You are safe here.
anomaly.4157.b: Your home planet was ruined by the war, only you remain.
anomaly.4157.c: We salvaged what we could of your ruined homeworld.
anomaly.4157.desc: The container found on [WarriorHomePlanet.GetName] turned out to be a cryogenic device! The preserved alien within has awoken. She speaks using telepathic concepts:\n\n"Why have you brought me back, captor? Is the war of my people over?"
anomaly.4157.name: Cryopod Warrior
anomaly.4158.desc: "I feared that this would happen. I only hope that my knowledge, and our failure as a species, can teach others."
anomaly.4158.f: Leave. Your fate is your own.
anomaly.4158.militant.b: To be frozen in war you must be of high value?
anomaly.4158.spiritual.b: Were you preserved for a divine mission?
anomaly.4158.xenophobe.f: You are of no use to us. Leave our planet!
anomaly.4159.desc: "So that's why... I feared that I would wake up to these news. To be honest I feared I would never wake at all. What does your kind want of me?"
anomaly.4160.desc: "Your words, and your civilization speaks to me, captor. I will join you, in hopes that you will learn from my people's mistakes.
anomaly.4161.desc: The way you speak. The way this room speaks for you. It tells me that our views do not align, captor. So no, I will not join you. I will return to [WarriorHomePlanet.GetName], and tell its stories for as long as I remain."
anomaly.4162.desc: "I would rather die!"\n\nMajula runs out of the room, enraged. As a crowd had gathered outside to take part in the proceedings she grabs a researcher to use as leverage. In the escape, the researcher dies before Majula is gunned down by security.
anomaly.4163.desc: "Farewell, captor. Try and learn from what happened to my people, lest we meet again and you too have ended up to be the last of your kind."
anomaly.4165.desc: Across the barren fields of [From.GetName] there are indications of old battles being fought. Beneath the lifeless ground our researchers on the [Root.GetName] have found bones, metallic shards and, most surprisingly, a container filled with documents.\n\nIf we send the documents to our homeworld for translation we could potentially learn more about this war and who fought in it. It would also be possible to simply sell them off as antiques.
anomaly.4165.name: Teachings of Warriors
anomaly.4166.a: Even the wise can go to war it seems.
anomaly.4166.a.tooltip: Gives access to the §Y$edict_masters_writings_war$§! Empire Edict.
anomaly.4166.desc: Our language experts have been at it for weeks to try and translate the documents we found in the old battlefield. Today we finally have some results. We now know that the fallen warriors all followed the teachings of a philosopher called "Telisa the Teller of Tales."\n\n$anomaly.4166.base.desc$
anomaly.4166.found.desc: It appears that the texts we found buried in the battlefield were more teachings written by "Telisa the Teller of Tales."\n\n$anomaly.4166.base.desc$
anomaly.4170.a.tooltip: Adds the §YRich Gas Deposits§! modifier to [From.GetName]:\n£energy£ §G+50%§!
anomaly.4170.basic.desc: $anomaly.4170.start.desc$\n\nHowever, using these resources would deplete them rather quickly, as the deposits are rare and small in size.
anomaly.4170.material.desc: $anomaly.4170.start.desc$\n\nThe potential gain this would serve to us because heavily outweighs any damage that could be caused to the environment.
anomaly.4170.name: Volatile Resources
anomaly.4172.conqueror.desc: The colony we took over used to hold rich resources of gas underneath the surface. Now they've depleted, reducing the energy output of our industries.
anomaly.4172.owner.desc: The energy rich gas found on one of our colonies has now depleted. The extra resource output has been lost, greatly increasing our need for new deposits to replace it.
anomaly.5.a: These ill-gotten gains shall serve us well.
anomaly.5.desc: This asteroid appears to have been used intermittently as a base by a band of alien pirates roughly one thousand years ago. By entering the base, we managed to recover their abandoned treasure hoard. It consisted largely of stolen trinkets and artifacts, but some of it still appears to be of value.
anomaly.5.name: Pirate Treasure
anomaly.50.desc: Asteroid [From.GetName] is pockmarked with craters from weapon blasts, and appears to have been used as a target range by someone roughly two millennia ago. Residual energy readings suggest they tested increasingly exotic weaponry, including subspace bombs and some kind of singularity generator. Our scientists would be interested in studying the unusual energy echoes that remain.
anomaly.50.name: Weapons Target Range
anomaly.5000.desc: The [Root.GetName] has picked up some curious readings from [From.GetName]. There are significant pockets of radiation in the gas giant's atmosphere that appear to be the result of intense orbital bombardment. What someone could hope to gain by bombing a gas giant from orbit remains a mystery however.\n\nAs the [Root.GetName] was preparing to break orbit, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] discovered a weak signal coming from the planet's interior. It may be a transmission of some kind, but the gas giant's background radiation makes it difficult to isolate.
anomaly.5000.name: Gas Giant Signal
anomaly.5001.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has managed to isolate the weak signal that was coming from somewhere deep inside the atmosphere of [From.From.From.GetName]. It does indeed appear to be a transmission, and we have filtered it through our translation software.
anomaly.5002.desc: The weak signal we picked up coming from the interior of the gas giant [From.From.From.GetName] has faded. We shall never learn of its origin.
anomaly.5003.a: If you have no technology, how are we speaking?
anomaly.5003.c: You want us to transport your entire species to another planet?
anomaly.5003.desc: Finally! Well met, spacefarer! We are the Dathnak, and the planet you are orbiting is Tollok Rong - our ancestral home. It is always riveting to meet a solid, even if our last encounter with your kind was somewhat... problematic.\n\nYou have no doubt detected the radiation surges coming from our atmosphere. Tollok Rong is dying, and our species will perish unless we find a new home. We have identified a planet that would suit our physiology, but we have no means to get there. Sadly, our non-corporeal nature means we don't have much in the way of industry or technology. Will you help us?
anomaly.5003.e: Sorry. It would be too much of a hassle.
anomaly.5003.name: Gas Giant Transmission
anomaly.5004.desc: Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has finished supervising the relocation of the Dathnak to their new home. A convoy of civilian freighters equipped with massive pressurized gas tanks ferried the gaseous beings across space and deposited them into the gas giant's atmosphere. Their ancient transmitter and scanner array were also brought along.
anomaly.5005.desc: The conditions on Tollok Rong have deteriorated to the point where the Dathnak can no longer be saved. The radiation has spread across most of the atmosphere, and the Dathnak survivors have retreated even deeper towards the planet's core where communication with the surface is no longer possible. Eventually the radiation will finds its way there as well, rendering their species extinct.
anomaly.5006.a.2: Baldarak? That is an excellent name!
anomaly.5006.b: Good luck with your new home.
anomaly.5006.desc: We are forever in your debt! This planet has exceeded our expectations. For the first time in generations, our young can frolic in the upper atmosphere without starting to glow.\n\nWe have decided to call our new home Baldarak after your species. Future generations of Dathnak shall always know the name of their saviors!
anomaly.5007.a: Well, as long as it's just another gas giant...
anomaly.5007.b: Absolutely not. Our deal was to transport you to ONE planet.
anomaly.5007.desc: Hello again! You will be pleased to learn that our species has quadrupled in number since we arrived! Many of us were swept up in a festive mood when we made planetfall, and things got a bit frisky to say the least.\n\nAfter the positive experience we had colonizing Baldarak, a few brave pioneers have asked me to petition you for passage to another gas giant. We have already located a promising candidate within your space that would be suitable for colonization. What do you say, friends?
anomaly.5007.name: A New Colony
anomaly.5008.a: Make the most of it, Dathnak.
anomaly.5008.desc: As before, a convoy of freighters was assembled to safely transport the Dathnak colonists inside pressurized gas tanks. After a brief journey, they successfully made planetfall on the gas giant which they have named "New Baldarak." A satellite was left in orbit to allow for long-range communication with Baldarak.
anomaly.5009.desc: Greetings from New Baldarak! Things are progressing well here at our new colony. However, we have a small request...\n\nChabky Raddh, one of our colonists, misses her family and friends on Baldarak terribly and wants to go home. Her whining is driving us crazy! If it's not too much to ask, do you think you could take her back?
anomaly.5009.name: Chabky Raddh
anomaly.5010.desc: A single cargo tug hauling a gas canister has arrived at Baldarak under escort by the [Root.GetName]. The contents of the canister have been released into the gas giant's atmosphere, safely returning the Dathnak colonist to her home.
anomaly.5011.a: We shall dispatch a ship at once.
anomaly.5011.b: Enough! We are not your errand boys.
anomaly.5011.desc: We bring alarming news, [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName] friends!\n\nContact with our colony on New Baldarak has been lost! They no longer respond to any of our satellite transmissions, and we fear the worst. Perhaps the aliens who bombarded our original homeworld have returned to finish the job. Please send a ship to investigate!
anomaly.5011.name: Lost Contact
anomaly.5012.a: Open a channel to the planet.
anomaly.5012.desc: Our investigation of New Baldarak has revealed nothing out of the ordinary. The satellite the colony used to communicate with their capital is still functional as far as we can tell.
anomaly.5013.a: Tell us what you have planned.
anomaly.5013.c: We are not getting involved in your internal dispute.
anomaly.5013.desc:
Greetings from the New Baldarak Revolutionary Front!

We have thrown off the yoke of oppression and are at last free from the tyranny of Baldarak! We have no quarrel with you, [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName], as long as you refrain from aiding the Baldarak imperialists in their inevitable attempt to crush our revolution.

You could help us take the fight to our enemies, however... would you be willing to deliver one of our commando units to Baldarak?
anomaly.5013.name: Revolutionary Front
anomaly.5014.b: You need to solve your own problems.
anomaly.5014.desc:
I speak on behalf of the lawful Dathnak government on Baldarak.

We have received a manifesto from the group that seized control of New Baldarak, and boy, what a bunch of hogwash! These brigands and anarchists are a terrible embarrassment to us, [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesName]. Will you help us stomp out their little "revolution" before it spreads here and someone actually gets hurt?

General Paltanak has prepared an expeditionary force to retake the colony, but we'll need your help transporting it there.
anomaly.5014.name: Baldarak Responds
anomaly.5015.a: We shall see what happens next.
anomaly.5015.desc: A cargo tug escorted by the [Root.GetName] has stealthily dropped the cargo pod containing the revolutionary commando unit into Baldarak's atmosphere. Moments later, flashes can be seen coming from deep within the gas giant's cloud layer. Could it be signs of fighting?
anomaly.5016.a: Perhaps everything will work out for the best.
anomaly.5016.desc:
This is Citizen Fotanga! The people of Baldarak have overthrown the tyrants and oppressors that sought to enslave our species under their rule. A revolutionary council has been established to see our great nation through this transitional phase, while we work diligently to restore freedom to the people.

We wish to thank our comrades in the [Root.GetName] for their assistance in making this day come true.

That is all.
anomaly.5016.name: The Revolutionary Council
anomaly.5017.b: Enough. Block all future transmissions from these creatures.
anomaly.5017.desc:
This is Citizen Fotanga! The People's Revolutionary Council has unanimously voted to rename the planet formerly known as "Baldarak" to "Fotangia" in honor of my leadership.

Also, the planet formerly known as "New Baldarak" shall henceforth be known as "Chabkymak" after Chabky Raddh, our Minister of Public Safety.

That is all.
anomaly.5017.name: Baldarak Public Announcement
anomaly.5018.desc:
This is Citizen Fotanga! The People's Revolutionary Council wishes to announce the impending execution of 4,539 individuals convicted of state treason and counter-revolutionary activities.

Let this serve as a warning to all those who would stand in the way of our glorious revolution.

That is all.
anomaly.5019.desc:
This is Citizen Rutmag! The People's Revolutionary Council wishes to announce the impending execution of Former Citizen Fotanga, who has been convicted of demagoguery, corruption and general incompetence.

I will be assuming all of his former duties. My first decree is that the original names of planets Fotangia and Chabkymak be restored.

That is all.
anomaly.5020.a: Now we wait and see what happens next.
anomaly.5020.desc: Several freighters under escort by the [Root.GetName] have dropped the cargo canisters carrying the Dathnak expeditionary force into New Baldarak's atmosphere. Moments later flashes can be seen coming from beneath the gas giant's cloud layer. The fighting appears to have started.
anomaly.5021.desc:
General Paltanak here, speaking from New Baldarak. Operation Gaseous Fury has been a complete success. All primary objectives have been seized, and government control has been restored to all atmospheric sectors.

Aside from a few holdouts, most rebel units have surrendered or been routed. Much obliged for the support, [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]. If you'll excuse me, I need to transmit a casualty report to Baldarak.

Paltanak out.
anomaly.5021.name: Expeditionary Force Seizes Control
anomaly.5022.desc:
General Paltanak here, acting military governor of New Baldarak. I am pleased to announce the end of major combat operations in sector 47-G.  At least 512 insurgents have been confirmed killed since the operation began two cycles ago, while our own losses have been minimal.

Extra commendations to all forces involved for keeping civilian casualties at an acceptable level.

Paltanak out.
anomaly.5022.name: New Baldarak Announcement
anomaly.5023.desc:
This is General Paltanak, military governor of New Baldarak. I wish to address unsubstantiated reports claiming there has been a resurgence in rebel activity on this world. Let me tell you now that nothing could be further from the truth.

This planet has been fully pacified, and all subversive terrorist elements have been fully rooted out. Its citizens are once again productive members of the greater Dathnak nation.

Paltanak out.
anomaly.5024.desc:
Colonel Rapzak reporting, acting military governor of New Baldarak. I must regretfully inform the galactic community of the demise of my predecessor, General Paltanak. After being lured into a dastardly ambush by rebel forces, the General gave his life in the finest tradition of the service.

A state funeral with full honors will be held at the successful conclusion of our current offensive against the rebel strongholds.

Rapzak out.
anomaly.5025.desc: [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]! I have been asked to approach you on behalf of the Baldarak Science Academy. Although we Dathnak don't possess much in the way of technology, we are certainly capable of higher reasoning!\n\nA few of our think tanks have spent the last several years studying theoretical physics, and we would like to share their findings. Perhaps the data will be of some use to you in the empire building activities you solids are so fond of.
anomaly.5025.name: Baldarak Science Academy
anomaly.5026.a: Yes, we will dispose of these minerals for you...
anomaly.5026.desc: Hello, [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]!\n\nWould you be willing to do us a favor? Baldarak's strong gravity well pulls all kinds of trash into our atmosphere, and at a recent council meeting we decided to step up our cleaning efforts. One of our reclamation units came across a discarded cargo pod, and we're wondering if you'd be willing to help us dispose of it. It seems to contain large quantities of various worthless metals.
anomaly.5026.name: Spring Cleaning
anomaly.55.desc: Upon closer examination, we have discovered that a smaller asteroid consisting almost entirely of precious metals recently collided with [From.GetName]. This small but dense cache of metals was hidden just beneath the asteroid's surface, but now that it has been discovered it should be accessible to mining.
anomaly.55.name: Asteroid Collision
anomaly.60.desc: This particular asteroid is an extrasolar capture, and appears to have been washed by some kind of exotic radiation as it plummeted through interstellar space before finally settling in the [From.GetStarName] system. The original source of this radiation remains unknown, but the [Root.GetName] has been able to pick up a wealth of physics data by studying the asteroid's energy emissions.
anomaly.60.name: Exotic Radiation
anomaly.600.desc: A large mineral-rich asteroid collided with [From.GetName] at some point during the previous thousand years in what must have been a major impact event. An abundance of minerals can now be found on the [From.GetPlanetMoon] in the vicinity of the impact crater.
anomaly.600.name: Asteroid Collision
anomaly.6005.name: Abnormal Conditions
anomaly.605.desc: A massive crater on [From.GetName] appears to be the result of a collision with a starship. From the size of the crater, we suspect that a ship exiting a hyperlane at maximum velocity rammed the [From.GetPlanetMoon] for reasons unknown roughly 10,000 years ago.\n\nThe [Root.GetName] has picked up residual subspace echoes near the crash site reminiscent of a collapsed hyperparticulate field, but as the ship itself disintegrated on impact the theory cannot be verified.
anomaly.605.name: FTL Impact
anomaly.610.desc: A microsingularity recently intersected [From.GetName], passing straight through the core and emerging on the other side of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]. The encounter does not seem to have caused any permanent damage, but it has altered the energy output of the planetary core slightly in a way that defies our current scientific models. Further study may be warranted.
anomaly.610.name: Microsingularity
anomaly.615.desc: The magnetic field of [From.GetName] experienced a complete reversal while it was being observed by the [Root.GetName]. This rare event has interchanged the positions of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s magnetic poles. Fortunately, it was all recorded by the sensors of our ship, providing our scientists with a lot of valuable data.
anomaly.615.name: Magnetic Reversal
anomaly.625.desc: The mummified remains of a single individual belonging to a previously unknown mammalian species have been found drifting in high orbit over [From.GetName]. The being is dressed in what appears to be a flight suit complete with a helmet, and may be a fighter pilot that ejected in some ancient battle only to be forgotten and left behind. Our study of the corpse has provided some interesting data.
anomaly.625.name: Mummified Pilot
anomaly.630.desc: An abandoned life pod was detected in close orbit of §Y[From.GetName]§!. It is covered in scorch marks, presumably from when the pod's mothership exploded, and preliminary scans suggest it was built more than 5,000 years ago.\n\nThe crew of the [Root.GetName] managed to open the pod, revealing the withered remains of a reptilian alien clad in a resplendent uniform. Clutched in one of its claws was a small picture of another individual from the same race - possibly a mate or revered leader.
anomaly.630.name: Ancient Life Pod
anomaly.635.desc: Someone used a mining laser from orbit approximately five thousand years ago to carve a large body of writing into the surface of [From.GetName]. The massive script covers a large portion of the [From.GetPlanetMoon]'s upper hemisphere, and appears to be a short story chronicling the difficult life of an alien mercenary.
anomaly.635.name: Alien Writing
anomaly.65.desc: After identifying an anomaly in the gravity well of [From.GetName], the [Root.GetName] has discovered the shattered wreckage of an ancient ore superfreighter buried deep within the asteroid's crust. It must have carried a full load when it crashed, and the asteroid's mineral wealth has been revised accordingly.
anomaly.65.name: Crashed Ore Freighter
anomaly.650.desc: We have discovered an abandoned solar sail ship in orbit around §Y[From.GetName]§!. The sublight vessel was built by an unknown culture, and appears to be several thousand years old. One of the massive sails has a large tear where some kind of object passed through - most likely a meteoroid - which appears to have disabled the vessel. Although the technology of the ship is severely outdated, it does possess some interesting engineering design choices.
anomaly.650.name: Solar Sailer
anomaly.655.desc: While approaching §Y[From.GetName]§!, the §Y[Root.GetName]§! suddenly received a glancing hit by several passing mass driver rounds. The projectiles were billions of years old, and based on their trajectory they appear to be stray rounds fired from a neighboring galaxy. After missing their intended target, they continued on their journey for untold millennia - until today. The rounds we have recovered are of an advanced design despite their incredible age.
anomaly.655.name: Glancing Hit
anomaly.660.desc: For some reason, someone has towed an asteroid into a stable orbit around §Y[From.GetName]§!. The massive engine sections and braking thrusters can still be found on the surface, although they have long since been rendered inoperable. Whoever did this also mined the asteroid for minerals, but these operations were seemingly abandoned shortly after they begun.
anomaly.660.name: Towed Asteroid
anomaly.670.desc: Our survey of §Y[From.GetName]§! has revealed that it used to be a pristine continental [From.GetPlanetMoon] with a mild climate as little as a thousand years ago. In stark contrast, the atmosphere today is extremely toxic, the surface highly irradiated and the world has long since lost the ability to support life.\n\nWe have detected signs that the [From.GetPlanetMoon] was the scene of an incredibly destructive thermonuclear war waged between factions of a relatively advanced indigenous pre-space civilization.
anomaly.670.name: Nuclear Devastation
anomaly.6700.desc:
As the [Root.GetName]s' crew explored the barren dunes of §H[nanite_swarm_planet.GetName]§!, the first reports were much as expected: this is an unnatural wasteland with no signs of life above the water's surface. Yet the planet's aquatic life has evolved well past the point we would expect some species to make forays onto dry land.

Additionally, the crew discovered what originally appeared to be various ancient-looking, sand-covered structures. Shortly after they began digging into these apparent buildings, small swarms of nanites emerged and began harassing the researchers. It seems the buildings are formed not from sand, but by billions of microscopic nanomachines!

Once mobilized, these swarms quickly multiplied, awakening more and more of the dormant whole. [Root.GetLeaderName] ordered a swift evacuation of the planet, allowing the [Root.GetName] just enough time to escape the atmosphere with a swarming storm of nanites in hot pursuit. The remaining swarm now seems agitated, and it's not calming down.
anomaly.6700.name: Narrow Escape
anomaly.6705.b.tooltip: Direct our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] to unlock the secrets of the evolved nanites on [nanite_swarm_planet.GetName]
anomaly.6705.name: On the Origin of Nanites
anomaly.6710.c: These are not mere automatons, but living beings!
anomaly.6710.name: Artificial Immune System
anomaly.6715.a: Start up the colony ships' engines!
anomaly.6715.desc: While the nanite swarm of §H[nanite_swarm_planet.GetName]§! was impressive as a collective, as individuals they were quite vulnerable. Extracting a few from the planet's atmosphere and using our advanced AI technology, we have managed to reprogram the communication systems of the machines. Then when we reintroduced our reprogrammed nanites into the swarm, the modifications spread across the globe in a flash.\n\nWith control of the network secured, our first order was to reintroduce a stable biosphere onto §H[nanite_swarm_planet.GetName]§! - one which is optimized for [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]. The planet is now ready and waiting for us, and the nanite swarm is prepared to help with any task our colonists may give it.
anomaly.6715.name: Fertilization of Nanites
anomaly.6720.desc: The dust is settling after the [root.fleet.GetName] finished orbital bombardment of §H[nanite_swarm_planet.GetName]§!. Despite using a mix of powerful explosives and experimental EMPs, the process took a long time - but at last, there is no longer any trace of machine life down there.\n\nOur future colonists will have access to these gnats' remains and will, hopefully, manage to harvest something valuable from them.
anomaly.6720.name: No One Outsmarts Orbital Bombardment
anomaly.6725.desc: Our precautions and special equipment were not enough. Shortly after establishing a colony on §H[nanite_swarm_planet.GetName]§!, we lost contact with our teams on the ground. The last communication we received from the settlement showed a sky darkened by small black bodies swarming the outpost.
anomaly.6725.name: Underprepared
anomaly.6740.a: Send the new frequencies back to our artists.
anomaly.6740.a.gestalt: Retrieve these new frequencies for further analysis.
anomaly.6740.b: Harvest the crystal to insulate our energy weapons.
anomaly.6740.desc:
The cause of the solar radiation resonance observed around the corona of §Y[From.GetName]§! turned out to be an unusual crystal formation capable of enduring the heat!

Having brought the crystal aboard, our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] were startled to realize that the strange resonance was reproducible. First, they exposed the crystal to the same solar radiation from [From.GetName], producing an identical result to the initially recorded phenomenon. It also seemed to create resonances with all energy waves we sent through it, forming new colors and sounds never before observed by [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural]!

Such frequencies could change the way we view the universe. Alternatively, we can develop research applications for a crystalline structure capable of surviving the intense heat of a star.
anomaly.6740.name: The Color of Science
anomaly.6745.b: Another exoplanet added to our growing list.
anomaly.6745.desc: For as long as we [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] have been able to look to the stars for new homes, [From.GetName] has been a naive dream: a place we would look to with optimism; a new home. Sadly as our telescopes got better, we realized that the planet would probably be a tidally locked, frozen hellscape - a theory which we have confirmed today.\n\nThere is hope, however; this world has all the building blocks necessary for a habitable planet. It might just need a slight push...
anomaly.6745.name: [From.GetName]
anomaly.6750.desc: This tidally locked planet appears to have all the building blocks for a habitable world. Perhaps there is something that can be built here.
anomaly.6750.name: [From.GetName]
anomaly.6755.a: We will try to identify the signal destination.
anomaly.6755.b: Bring them back to be sold.
anomaly.6755.c: We don't have time for this.
anomaly.6755.desc: Below the surface of [From.GetName] lives a most peculiar organism. Scans and samples show that it is some sort of mycelium littered with spores. Compared to the traditional size of spores on our homeworld, these are massive. Their surface is a shimmering kaleidoscope, and the hues seem to change based on their surroundings.\n\nThe strangest thing about them is that they seem to form a network capable of generating what the science crew believes could be a signal. The current emissions are very weak, but with some effort, it might be possible to find out where they lead.
anomaly.6755.name: Fungal Emitters
anomaly.6760.a: Prepare a project to do so.
anomaly.6760.desc: $anomaly.6760.intro$\n\nOur scientists hypothesize that we might be capable of strengthening the current network by bringing some of these spores back to the 'Fumongus'.
anomaly.6765.desc: $anomaly.6760.intro$\n\nSince we dismantled the network, we don't really have a practical use for this information.
anomaly.6770.desc: $anomaly.6770.intro$ Our puzzled scientist finally managed by 'using mushrooms to peer into additional dimensions.' Details are scarce about what this entails, but in any case: the operation was a success and has pointed us towards a destination.
anomaly.6770.name: Following the Fungi
anomaly.6780.desc: $anomaly.6770.intro$ Despite the best efforts of [Root.GetLeaderName], it was impossible to determine a destination for the signal and the mycelium mostly remains a mystery. Despite this, we managed to learn a lot in the process and the data is being brought back as we speak.
anomaly.6785.desc: Grafting the mutated spores onto the existing mushroom was a feat of bio-engineering. With the help of archives detailing the genetic alterations already made on the 'Fumongus,' our scientists managed to further alter it without compromising its efficiency. The results were spectacular, and in a matter of months, the mushrooms had grown tenfold. This in turn increased the need for water to supply them, but the nearby frozen asteroids hold enough to hydrate them for centuries, if not millennia.\n\nWith bigger mushrooms came a better network, and after some upgrades to the computing equipment, we are now once again ready to listen to what the spores have to say.
anomaly.6785.name: Mushrooming the Network
anomaly.6786.desc: We have found a bipedal robot floating in space. Its faceplate is featureless, and its metal exterior is damaged. Preliminary scans indicate it has residual power, but its power source is radically different from our own. Its internal circuitry may hold memories of its previous existence, but recharging it and translating its information will take time.
anomaly.6786.name: Lost Soul
anomaly.6787.desc: Through diligent effort, we have found a way to recharge the robot's power supply and scan its memory banks. Sadly, the machine has deteriorated so badly that we cannot retrieve coherent information. We will consider a follow-up study, and we may search for others of its kind, but the fate of this mechanical castaway must remain a mystery.
anomaly.6787.name: Old Soul
anomaly.6788.desc: Our analysis of the temporal fluctuations in the [From.GetStarName] system has revealed something remarkable: a massive prism, floating in space. Rather than light, the prism refracts time. Depending on the angle of incidence, the crew of the [Root.GetName] report experiencing time at different rates. Scans indicate that some have aged rapidly, while others are days, or even years younger than they should be.\n\nWhile our study of the prism has certainly deepened our understanding of the nature and properties of time, its origin and purpose remain a mystery.
anomaly.6788.name: Temporal Prism
anomaly.6791.name: Ghost Ship
anomaly.6793.name: Psionic Chatter
anomaly.6794.name: Look Who's Talking
anomaly.680.desc: 24,000 years ago §Y[From.GetName]§! had the misfortune of being directly in the path of a long gamma-ray burst from a collapsing star within our galaxy. The [From.GetPlanetMoon] was washed with lethal radiation, which not only produced acute radiation poisoning in most life forms on the side of [From.GetName] that happened to be facing the burst, but also depleted much of the ozone layer.\n\nThis extinction event killed off an estimated 86% of all biota, including an early Bronze Age civilization whose ruins can still be found in some parts of the northern hemisphere. The biosphere is only now showing signs of recovery.
anomaly.680.name: Gamma-Ray Burst
anomaly.6800.desc: Our sensors have discovered that the ship remnants on [From.GetName] got there in a peculiar way. The ships seem to have been intentionally driven straight into the asteroid, probably from light-years away, to test the accuracy of the designers' thrusters. As we deep-scan the remains, we pick out one ship in particular, which seems to have reasonably intact propulsion.
anomaly.6800.name: Target Practice
anomaly.6805.desc: Hoping to discover rare resources inside [From.GetName], our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] stumbled upon something most unusual. What had appeared to be a simple asteroid was in fact a long-dormant relay station with complex electronics and advanced sensors set up to send signals back to an ancient empire. The impact also has damaged some of the asteroid's internal structure, and we can only extract one system from it.
anomaly.6805.name: Asteroid Sensor Relay
anomaly.6810.a: Send an away party, giant alien arthropoids are no joke!
anomaly.6810.b: It's probably for the best that we leave them alone.
anomaly.6810.d.tooltip: Use our advance knowledge of habitats to breach the station's atmosphere.
anomaly.6810.desc: We were wrong. The station orbiting [From.GetName] is not uninhabited; instead, it is crawling with giant alien arthropoids! The probes we deployed into the station only returned skittering shadows and large mandibles before signal was lost. Deep scans of the station have also revealed what we postulate to be an incredibly complex databank. To reach this databank, we would have to go through that cluster of many-legged defenders.
anomaly.6810.name: Infestation
anomaly.6815.a: Wait, so you are not a hostile infestation?
anomaly.6815.desc: Oh, hello there! Sorry about destroying your probe earlier. It's just that we are conducting some very delicate experiments here, and we were worried that outside interference could alter the results - I'm sure you understand. Now, how can we help you?
anomaly.6815.name: The Giant Alien Arthropoids
anomaly.6820.desc: What would ever give you that impression? We are a Curator detachment sent here to study this system's unique properties. If you wish to partake of our order's usual offerings, I suggest contacting the primary research lab. I can provide you with a copy of our findings so far.
anomaly.6825.name: Crystal Growths
anomaly.6835.a: Search for more asteroids to expand the crystal farms.
anomaly.6835.a.tooltip: Up to §Y3§! random asteroids will now produce §G3§! £food£ food.
anomaly.6835.b: Let's not expand the crystal farms.
anomaly.6835.desc: After eating space-based crystal sugars for a few years now, it has become apparent that our population would like to see it more readily available. Our [Root.GetScientistPlural] have come up with a list of potential candidates where we could construct more crystal farms.
anomaly.6835.name: Call for Crystals
anomaly.6840.b: Good things come to those who wait.
anomaly.6840.desc: [From.GetName] is a peculiar gas giant. Our knowledge of astrophysics tells us that the planet should have a planetary ring, yet it doesn't. The cause of this became apparent after our science ship took a closer look at the intriguing moon. The planet is surrounded by shepherd moons, all incredibly rich in minerals and accumulating more every year. We could blast the moons with precise and controlled explosions and harvest them or keep them inside the ring zone and harvest the space debris they accrue.
anomaly.6840.name: Too Few Sheep
anomaly.6845.desc: We did indeed discover life on [From.GetName], but by our actions, it has since been eradicated. The microbial creatures which lived in the outer edges of the gas giant's atmosphere reacted poorly to our deep scans. These frequencies caused each creature's cellular structure to resonate - an effect that then cascaded and spread from gas mite to gas mite. Each was rendered inert soon after.\n\nWe are now in orbit over the largest graveyard in the universe.
anomaly.6845.name: Cascading Catastrophe
anomaly.685.desc: There is evidence that the current climate of §Y[From.GetName]§! is the cause of a runaway greenhouse effect triggered by massive amounts of pollution. The oceans have boiled away and the [From.GetPlanetMoon] is permanently enclosed in a dense cloud layer due to the thick atmosphere.\n\nScattered ruins from the indigenous civilization can still be found on the surface, suggesting an overpopulated culture that perished in the mid to late stages of an Industrial Age.
anomaly.685.name: Runaway Greenhouse Effect
anomaly.6850.name: Reversing Deep Scan Polarities
anomaly.6855.b: Wait, [From.GetName] is even MORE interesting now.
anomaly.6855.desc.gestalt: The signals from [Root.GetName] were suddenly cut off from the consciousness. The [Owner.GetScientistPlural] do not appear to be dead, just unable to communicate with us. They had been studying the strange localized storms on [From.GetName] and were sending back incredible preliminary reports. The tempest reacted to the probes being sent in, creating vacuum pockets to avoid them and then slowly seeping back in towards the drones. The plan for [Root.GetName] was to test out numerous scanning frequencies at the storm before contact was cut off. The science ship seems to have sunk into the gas giant and now appears dormant.
anomaly.6855.desc.regular: The last signal received from [Root.GetName] was not much more than garbled static. They had been studying the strange localized storms on [From.GetName] and were sending back incredible preliminary reports. The tempest reacted to the probes being sent in, creating vacuum pockets to avoid them and then slowly seeping back in towards the drones. [Root.GetName] was planning on testing out numerous scanning frequencies at the storm before we lost contact. The science ship seems to have sunken into the gas giant and appears to be dormant.
anomaly.6855.name: Caught in the Eye
anomaly.6860.desc: After months of work, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] finally managed to alternate [FromFrom.GetName] shields in such a way that [FromFromFrom.GetName] tempest released its grip on the marooned ship. Communications with [trapped_in_storm.GetName] was quickly re-established, and incredibly none onboard [FromFrom.GetName] seem to remember their time trapped inside the storm.
anomaly.6860.name: Fluctuating Shield Frequencies
anomaly.6865.desc: Once [Root.GetName] got close enough to scan the cargo pod it was assumed that the sensors were malfunctioning. The pod is built out of the exact same [Owner.GetBioAlloy] we ourselves use for spacebound structures. The likelihood that some alien beings would come up with this exact mixture is beyond unlikely, yet after recalibrating the scanners the same results appeared.\n\nUpon opening the pod, the only thing greeting us was a collection of documents detailing exactly where we should assign each of our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] and what they should be asked to study. The instructions end on a fixed date, one that is scheduled to fall exactly 10 years from now.
anomaly.6865.name: Express Mail
anomaly.6870.a: Let our past selves deal with this.
anomaly.6870.desc: After years of uneasy development, a rip in the fabric of space has appeared above [Root.Capital.GetName]. Unnervingly this is the exact date as indicated in the strange instructions we received a decade ago. There is only one thing to do: send the documents we received back into the tear and close the loop.
anomaly.6870.name: Closing the Loop
anomaly.6875.desc: The asteroid around [From.GetName] has such a perfectly stable orbit that it's easy to understand why our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] thought it was placed there artificially. Yet, there are no conclusive indications of any propulsion systems or any other artificial marring. The only natural conclusion is that, by some absurdly improbable chance, the asteroid got caught in [From.GetName]'s gravity field. We have also detected some rare crystals on the surface of the asteroid.
anomaly.6875.name: Convenient Mining
anomaly.6880.desc: Just a day after finishing our mining station on the trapped asteroid, the rock abruptly rotated, destroying the mining station. In the process of doing this, even more rare crystals deposits were exposed to our sensors!
anomaly.6880.name: Unexplainable Rotations
anomaly.6885.desc: Warning sirens blared across [Solar_System.GetName] as the massive crystalline beast left the shelter of the asteroid we had been drilling into and extracting crystals from. It seems §Rangry§!.
anomaly.6885.name: Annoyed Crystal
anomaly.6890.a: What can we learn from it?
anomaly.6890.desc: The trapped asteroid is, in fact, a crystalline being's nest. It is good that we didn't keep digging, for it seems like we agitated the creature hibernating inside. If we do nothing for a while and study it from afar, it should settle down.
anomaly.6890.name: Sleeping Crystal Nest
anomaly.6895.desc.catano: The life signs observed within the toxic atmosphere of [From.GetName] are giant semi-organic machines! This alien industry seems to have been the cause of the noxious atmosphere on the planet, yet it's still operational. No other life signs remain on the world, and the creators of these machines must have left them running. We can't quite ascertain their purpose yet, but their construction could surely help our understanding of engineering.
anomaly.6895.desc.catayes: The life signs observed within the toxic atmosphere of [From.GetName] are giant semi-organic machines! Like us, it seems like the creators of this facility appreciated a merging of the biological and mechanical. This alien industry appears to have been the cause of the noxious atmosphere on the planet, yet it's still operational. No other life signs remain on the world, and the creators of these machines must have left them running. We can't quite ascertain their purpose yet, but their construction could surely help our understanding of engineering.
anomaly.6895.name: Toxic Biological Industry
anomaly.690.desc: Although toxic to most forms of known life, §Y[From.GetName]§! supports a thriving ecology within the high pressure of its atmosphere. Life here uses ammonia instead of water as a solvent, and has developed in ways that differ significantly from previously established ecological models. Its study would greatly benefit our knowledge of xeno biology.
anomaly.690.name: Ammonia Biosphere
anomaly.6900.a.tooltip: Use the world to assist in calculating our current astrophysics dilemmas.
anomaly.6900.desc: We didn't detect life forms below the surface. We detected them in the entire world! The frozen planet is interspersed with micro-thin tubes linked like a rudimentary computer. While the structure is primitive, its gigantic scale means it can probably rival some of [Owner.Capital.GetName]'s supercomputers in output. Even now, the computer seems to be active - our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] can interface with it, but since it's so slow, we would only be able to ask it a single question.
anomaly.6900.e: Best to observe it from afar.
anomaly.6900.name: Cool Thoughts
anomaly.6905.desc: Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have discovered something rather monstrous. The mountain range they scanned earlier was in actuality the outer membrane of a gigantic egg. It's uncertain what behemoth could lay such an egg and what horror would hatch from it.
anomaly.6905.name: Don't Count Your Planets
anomaly.6910.name: Galactic Omelet
anomaly.6915.desc.gestalt: Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] dispatched to the [Solar_System.GetName] system all reacted in alarm shortly before losing contact with the [Owner.GetBrainName], only telling us that §R"It's loose."§! The last transmission of the [Root.GetName] cuts off as the egg begins to crack open, and when we use our probes to scan the remains of [FromFromFrom.GetName], we find a hollow shell. It seems the creature had little gratitude for its liberator.
anomaly.6915.desc.regular: §R"IT LIVES! IT LIVES AGAIN! We are nothing but insignificant specks compared to such a creature; what does the ephemeral squabbling between empires matter in the face of such great-"§!\n\nThe last transmission of the [Root.GetName] cuts off there, and when we use our probes to scan the remains of [FromFromFrom.GetName], we find a hollow shell. It seems the creature had little gratitude to show its liberators.
anomaly.6915.name: Gratitude
anomaly.695.desc: Some kind of burrowing silicon-based life form inhabits a vast network of tunnels beneath the barren surface of [From.GetName]. As best as we can tell, the creatures feed off rocks and there is evidence to suggest that they possess a rudimentary form of intelligence. Their tunneling efforts have shuffled large amounts of valuable minerals to the surface.
anomaly.695.name: Silicon Life Forms
anomaly.7000.desc: The monolith we found on [From.GetName] dwarfs the science ship we sent to investigate it. A majestic, smooth slab of metal, the once-garish pigment patterns on the front have been reduced to mere flecks.\n\nA small power outlet on the machine's side promises its secrets will be unveiled in exchange for a modest sum of energy credits.
anomaly.7000.name: Mysterious Monolith
anomaly.7010.a: Patent the drink. Sell it to the whole galaxy.
anomaly.7010.desc.empty: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$The cylinder is empty, its content long evaporated through a corroded sealing cap. The container itself is still in good shape, though, and the unknown alloy is on par with the metal we use to make our ships.
anomaly.7010.desc.full.bio: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$ The drink has been easily replicated by our [Owner.GetScientistPlural], who, after conducting rigorous testing, have ascertained it to be safe, nutritious and - most crucially - delicious.
anomaly.7010.desc.full.megacorp: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$ According to our market data, the long-forgotten drink is 20% more delicious than our current range of drinkable products for biological entities.
anomaly.7010.desc.full.nonbio: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$$anomaly.7010.desc.full$ While the liquid provides no substance to us, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have been able to convert it into a much more valuable resource: §YExotic Gas§!.
anomaly.7010.desc.rot.bio: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$The cylinder contains a liquid most foul; a once-delicious nutrient long spoiled by time. By studying the substance, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] hope to learn about the biology of the aliens who once delighted in it - assuming we can do something about the smell first.
anomaly.7010.desc.rot.nonbio: $anomaly.7010.desc.base$The cylinder contains a liquid mixture of sucrose, citric acid, and other biological compounds. Our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] believe it to be a nutrient substance made by and for carbon-based beings. Further studies will hopefully provide more clues pertaining to the biology of this lost race.
anomaly.7010.name: The Machine Awakens
anomaly.7020.desc: We have found the wreckage of an archaic spaceship of unusual design. Instead of using propulsion similar to that of modern ships, the craft relied on large sails unfurled in the vacuum of space. Presumably, the ship harvested solar energy and drifted on the solar winds created by starlight.
anomaly.7020.name: On Solar Sails
anomaly.7030.desc: We have discovered an ancient alien starship half-buried in an asteroid crater. This science ship's exterior has an extensive sensory array and no weaponry. The exterior was not damaged in any way before it crashed. We can assume this catastrophe was the result of a fatal error caused by the crew.
anomaly.7030.name: Crash Site
anomaly.705.desc: A small short-range transmitter has been located on the surface of §Y[From.GetName]§!. It appears to be an ancient survey marker, placed here eons ago to mark a large deposit of precious metals. The miners it was meant for evidently never arrived, as the deposit is still here.
anomaly.705.name: Ancient Survey Marker
anomaly.7100.alt.desc: What our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] first mistook for asteroids have been revealed to be frozen, battered corpses of alien fauna, roughly matching the shape of the aliens seen roaming the system. The entire asteroid ring is, in fact, just an open burial ground. Some of the bodies we acquired are recently deceased, while others predate our empire by thousand of years.
anomaly.7100.desc: What our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] first mistook for asteroids have been revealed to be frozen, battered Tiyanki corpses reduced to shapeless lumps after decades in orbit. The entire asteroid ring is, in fact, just an open burial ground. Some of the bodies we acquired are recently deceased, while others predate our empire by thousand of years.
anomaly.7100.name: Open Burial
anomaly.7101.c.desc: The hive can replicate these magnetic waves and use them to strengthen its will.
anomaly.7101.hive.desc: The planet is emitting a series of signals that our exploratory drones speculated might be of artificial origin. Upon closer examination, they turned out to be nothing more than a natural phenomenon, one with the unusual property of strengthening the connection of our drones to the collective mind. It seems that drones exposed to the planet's magnetic waves respond better to the will of the hive.
anomaly.7101.machines.desc: The planet is emitting a series of signals that our exploratory drones speculated might be of artificial origin. Upon closer examination, the signals were revealed to be merely a natural phenomenon caused by unusual but harmless magnetic waves. This discovery does not provide any immediate benefit to the collective, but given their uniqueness, studying them may provide us with some research data in the long run.
anomaly.7101.name: Singing Planet
anomaly.7101.standard.desc: What we first assumed to be a deliberate attempt at communication has turned out to be an unusual but naturally occurring phenomenon. The magnetic waves produced by the planet, given proper handling and editing, may sound a bit like talking or even singing, but they are in no way created by a thinking being. Some of our scientists, however, find it quite catchy.\n\nIt might be possible to make use of this phenomenon, possibly by hosting artists or VIPs at a station created solely to catch these signals and play them as relaxing music.
anomaly.7105.desc:
The source of the unusual energy readings noted on [From.GetName] is confirmed to be a small, blue orb. The [Owner.GetScientistPlural] report that sensors pick up tachyons of reverse polarity.

Symbols are carved into the ground around the object, perhaps placed there by an older civilization. It is unclear whether they are meant as an instruction, or a warning.

The full inscription is far from translated, but individual symbols seem related to the measuring of time and the relative positions of celestial objects in the [Solar_System.GetName] system.
anomaly.7105.name: Concentrated Energy
anomaly.7110.desc: The orb of blue energy first detected on [FromFrom.GetName] has disappeared. A scan of the location show no traces of the strange sphere. Even more baffling is the erasure of the markings on the ground: it is as if they were never there.\n\nGiven the unusual tachyon readings we detected at the site, our [Owner.GetScientistPlural] postulate that both the orb and the writing were moving backwards through time.
anomaly.7110.name: Local Time Reversal
anomaly.7115.desc.devouring:
[Root.GetLeaderName] ate the blue orb on [FromFrom.GetName].

[leader.GetHeSheCap] received a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, we were certain that time would no longer affect [Root.GetLeaderName]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, we could use [leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [leader.GetHisHer] own.
anomaly.7115.desc.hive:
While working at the site on [FromFrom.GetName], [Root.GetLeaderName] brushed against the blue orb.

[leader.GetHeSheCap] received a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, we were certain that time would no longer affect [Root.GetLeaderName]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, we could use [leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [leader.GetHisHer] own.
anomaly.7115.desc.immortal:
While working at the site on [FromFrom.GetName], junior [Owner.GetScientist] [intemporal_leader.GetName] brushed against the blue orb.

[intemporal_leader.GetHeSheCap] later described a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [intemporal_leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [intemporal_leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [intemporal_leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, [intemporal_leader.GetName] was certain that time would no longer affect [intemporal_leader.GetHimHer]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, [intemporal_leader.GetHeShe] want[intemporal_leader.GetSXX] to use [intemporal_leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [intemporal_leader.GetHisHer] own.
anomaly.7115.desc.regular:
While working at the site on [FromFrom.GetName], [Root.GetLeaderName] brushed against the blue orb.

[leader.GetHeSheCap] later described a vision of time stretching out like a river into the infinite future and past. In front of [leader.GetHimHer], blue energy arced out of the timestream and was absorbed by [leader.GetHisHer] body. Although the incident was accurately measured by the other [Owner.GetScientistPlural] to span less than a second, [leader.GetHeShe] experienced it for more than a hour.

After the vision ended, [Root.GetLeaderName] was certain that time would no longer affect [leader.GetHimHer]. With an infinite lifetime ahead, [leader.GetHeShe] want[leader.GetSXX] to use [leader.GetHisHer] endless time to explore the universe on [leader.GetHisHer] own.
anomaly.7115.name: Time Flows Like a River
anomaly.7120.desc.hive:
Long-range scans picked up an approaching vessel near [Root.Capital.GetName]. As it moved closer, it became clear that the ship's design matched our own from a century ago. We discovered that the ship was piloted by [intemporal_explorer.GetName], the [Owner.GetScientist] who [intemporal_explorer.GetWasWere] detached from the timestream by a blue energy orb.

Again with us, knowledge flowed from the [Owner.GetScientist] into the collective: sense-impressions of colliding neutron stars and inverse space-time gravitational wells. Once the transfer was complete, the ship continued on into the dark. Remarkably, our physics [Owner.GetScientistPlural] have confirmed that much of this data is not only verifiable, but indeed groundbreaking.

[intemporal_explorer.GetName] appeared physically unchanged by the passage of time, but even our current technology could not explain the functionality of the orb. Barring their own fatal destruction, [intemporal_explorer.GetHeShe] will continue to explore the universe until the end of time.
anomaly.7120.desc.regular:
Long-range scans picked up an approaching vessel near [Root.Capital.GetName]. As it moved closer, it became clear that the ship's design matched our own from a century ago.

After opening comms, we discovered that the ship was piloted by [intemporal_explorer.GetName], the [Owner.GetScientist] who [intemporal_explorer.GetWasWere] detached from the timestream by a blue energy orb.

[intemporal_explorer.GetHeSheCap] rambled about colliding neutron stars and inverse space-time gravitational wells, before taking the ship back into the dark. Remarkably, our physicists have confirmed that much of this information is not only verifiable, but indeed groundbreaking.

[intemporal_explorer.GetName] appeared physically unchanged by the passage of time, but even our current technology could not explain the functionality of the orb. Barring their own fatal destruction, [intemporal_explorer.GetHeShe] will continue to explore the universe until the end of time.
anomaly.7120.name: The Return
anomaly.75.b: Make do with what you can study from the surface.
anomaly.75.c: It is not so unlike us. Let us talk.
anomaly.75.c.tooltip: Order [Root.GetName] to attach surface probes to [From.GetName] and decode its alleged neural activity
anomaly.75.desc: A scan of the particularly massive asteroid [From.GetName] yields fascinating results. The rock's core is shot through with a network of conductive crystals carrying a weak electric charge. The crew on the [Root.GetName] recognize this matrix as a primitive neural lattice and believe the celestial body to be thinking in some capacity, if not fully sapient. They seek permission to excavate the core and transport it to the nearest orbital station for closer study.
anomaly.75.name: Rock Brain
anomaly.76.a: On second thought, this seems ill-advised.
anomaly.76.a.tooltip: Abort any attempts at contacting [rock_brain.GetName] directly, and study it from afar
anomaly.76.desc: [rock_scientist.GetName] here. It was a challenge, but I think we've managed to parse the readings into something like... not language perhaps, but concepts. Ideas. And we can feed something similar back to the asteroid, to maybe communicate.\n\nWe'll display some of the §Y<filtered output>§!, and I'll do my best to give a more §G"§!complete interpretation§G"§! of the raw data.
anomaly.77.a: <Do you understand that we are not you?>
anomaly.77.b: <How long have you been drifting in orbit of [rock_sun.GetName]?>
anomaly.77.c: "Are we getting anything useful out of this?"
anomaly.77.desc:
§Y<new> <thoughts>. <reason>. <reason> <perplexing>.§!


§G"§!To provide some context, [rock_brain.GetName] has no sensory organs in the traditional sense. It is perceiving our input as its own thoughts. To an extent.§G"§!
anomaly.78.a: <Is there anything we can do to help you?>
anomaly.78.desc:
§Y<quer--. <query>§!


§G"§!As I feared. Our probes are bleeding [rock_brain.GetName] of the energy that drives its cognition. [rock_brain.GetName] is not a perfectly closed system so this would have happened eventually - though in tens of thousands of years, rather than now...§G"§!
anomaly.79.a: Was it the last of its kind, or the first?
anomaly.79.desc: [rock_brain.GetName] is silent. All attempts by Science Officer [rock_scientist.GetName] to recharge the mineral lattice within the asteroid have failed; whatever spark of sapience once animated its rough-hewn neurons is gone, but we have learned much from this distant evolutionary cousin.
anomaly.80.a: The crystals are still valuable in their own right.
anomaly.80.desc: The core of [From.From.GetName], once coaxed from beneath the crust of the asteroid, does not respond well to the vacuum of space. The [Root.GetName]'s instruments read a sudden energy spike moments before the rocky lump gently, but decisively, fractures.\n\nLarge chunks of the conductive mineral are salvaged, but whatever spectral charge animated them is now gone.
anomaly.80.name: Rock Migraine
anomaly.81.desc: Our necromancers have scored new traces across the asteroid's delicate mineral seams, crude invocations hewn in stone and suffused with a pulsing current. Yet, the consciousness that was [rock_brain.GetName] remains lost to us.\n\nIt is something different now, suspended in a sinister dream - fitted with directional thrusters and awaiting our command.
anomaly.85.a: Use the data to further research long-range communications.
anomaly.85.desc: Irregular electromagnetic bursts from [From.GetName] and its neighboring planets intrigue the crew of the [Root.GetName]. Further study reveals that the bursts are coded communications, though the contents are fairly banal. The electromagnetic activity suddenly ceases, as if in response to the eavesdropping, but not before the [Root.GetName] has cataloged the self-reported statuses of [From.GetName] and every other planet in the system.
anomaly.85.name: Gossiping Planets
anomaly.90.desc: The dense grasses of [From.GetName] respond to the [Root.GetName]'s exploratory probes by disassembling them in a spectacularly violent manner. As sinewy vines reach for the ship far above, the relative lack of animal life on the planet starts making sense.\n\nA §YSpecial Project§! has been issued for further study of the planet's plant life.
anomaly.90.name: Grasping Vines
anomaly.91.desc: Careful examination reveals that the violent behavior of the vines and grasses of [From.From.GetName] is no dumb self-defense reflex.\n\nThe plants have a complex internal social order. Depending on geographical region, different phyla assume a number of different tasks, the most important one seemingly being staving off native herbivores and would-be invaders from the skies.
anomaly.91.name: Grassy Militia
anomaly.95.a: It might make a good coaster for my drink.
anomaly.95.b.tooltip: Adds the coordinates of the Sol system to the Situation Log.\n
anomaly.95.c: I'm sure someone would be willing to pay for it.
anomaly.95.desc: An aluminum plaque is found drifting among the detritus around [From.GetName], its anodized surface standing out from the metal debris surrounding it. It depicts two ridiculous-looking mammalian figures and some rather tasteless geometric shapes.
anomaly.95.name: Important to Someone Else
anomaly.96.a.phile: You shouted into the void, and we came.
anomaly.96.a.phobe: Make a statement. Jettison the plaque into their sun.
anomaly.96.desc.neutral: The directions inferred from the inscribed plaque were largely accurate.\n\nThis is the system of Sol, with the plaque apparently originating from the planet our astronomers have labeled Sol III.
anomaly.96.desc.phile: We have finally reached the system of Sol, a destination some being went to great pains to communicate through a very primitive medium. The plaque's point of origin is seemingly the third rock from the sun, which should be a continental planet.
anomaly.96.desc.phobe: We have found the alleged source of the tacky metal scrap we recovered. The system of Sol is a pinprick in space centered on a pitiful yellow dwarf, a backwater completely eclipsed by the splendor of the [Root.Owner.GetName].
anomaly.96.name: Terra Firma
anomaly_failure.2670.desc: It appears as if the [Root.GetName]'s enthusiastic probing of the old construct's systems has, quite literally, backfired.\n\nBefore the ancient circuits finally fried, the [Root.GetName] managed to remotely activate the orbital station's positional thrusters - promptly knocking it out of its gentle orbit and into the star's gravity well. The mission's unfortunate outcome has had a profound impact on the ship's commander, [Root.GetLeaderName], who has grown from the experience.
anomaly_failure.4011.desc: Having searched the ship and inspected the crew's remains, Science Officer [Root.GetLeaderName] has deduced that the crewmembers must have killed each other. The solitude and confinement of space travel can break even the strongest of minds.
anomaly_failure.4012.desc: We are receiving a distress signal from the [Root.GetName]. The crew has gone mad and are killing each other! The captain has lost all control, sending help would be futile at this point. Could this have anything to do with that derelict ship they recently investigated?
anomaly_failure.4031.a: The rage of the machine is worth fearing.
anomaly_failure.4031.desc: We were unable to stall the fleet AI on [From.From.GetName]. Their ancient ships are taking to the skies and beyond, looking for the next battle according to their programmed parameters.
anomaly_failure.4037.desc: The radiation readings indicate that this is not the solar system we were looking for.
anomaly_failure.4066.desc: We could not stop the rampaging drill before it was too late. It dug too deep and was eventually crushed under the weight of rocky detritus of its own creation.
anomaly_failure.4081.desc: Bad news from the repairs project on [From.From.From.GetName]. The construction workers have not been able to fix the broken machine, as it has started to break down even further and seems to be beyond repair.
anomaly_failure.4086.desc: Sadly we were not able to save the drifting ship close to [From.From.From.GetName] before it was too late. An untracked asteroid appeared on a collision course and smashed the ship to pieces.
anomaly_failure.4116.desc: A last transmission has been received from the monster-infested ship. It tells us that the beast succeeded in getting through to the crew's hiding place.\n\nThe horrid encounter was far too graphic to describe. There were no survivors.
anomaly_failure.4136.desc: Sadly our linguists have been unable to understand the entirety of the alien language used in the old documents found on [From.From.From.GetName]. However, they managed to translate the essentials, which has given us a glimpse into the culture they originated from.
anomaly_failure.4156.desc: Fighting off the beasts around the underground vault on [WarriorHomePlanet.GetName] has caused the complex to collapse. We are unable to salvage anything of value from the debris.
anomaly_failure.4157.maxed.desc: $anomaly_failure.4157.base$.\n\nWhile not being that useful to us, there were also data on the civilization's culture and history, which could give us more insight into who they were.
anomaly_failure.4158.a.tooltip: §YYour Empire§! gains the §RFertility Inhibiting Bio-Weapon§! modifier.
anomaly_failure.4158.desc: After opening the container we found on [WarriorHomePlanet.GetName] we were shocked to realize that it was a dispenser for a biological weapon!\n\nThe bio-weapon was made to target fertility functions and quickly spreads. It is however not entirely compatible with our DNA, and will not cause us to diminish in numbers.
anomaly_failure.4170.basic.desc: $anomaly_failure.4170.base.desc$\n\nThe people who died in the explosion won't be forgotten.
anomaly_failure.4170.individ.desc: $anomaly_failure.4170.base.desc$\n\nThis backlash cannot be allowed to be repeated.
apoc.1.b.desc: We have encountered another abandoned Gateway, this time in the §H[gateway_system.GetName]§! system. Unlike the previous one, this Gateway has not been altered in any obvious way and our scans indicate that it is still connected to the rest of the network. However, it is currently inoperable due to its poor condition.
apoc.1.desc: An ancient space station of some kind has been located at the edge of the [gateway_system.GetName] system. The strong residual subspace signature that surrounds the station indicates that it may be a "§HGateway§!" of sorts - part of a theoretical network of similar stations that at some point would have allowed for near-instantaneous travel between different parts of the galaxy.\n\nAssuming this is a Gateway, its current state of disrepair has rendered it unusable. If it could be restored into working order, its owner would potentially be able to access any other functional gateways in the galaxy, enabling travel across huge distances in a matter of days.
apoc.1.name: Abandoned Gateway
apoc.10.a: Something might come through at any time!
apoc.10.name: Gateway Reactivated
apoc.100.desc.milit: Previously spoken of only in hushed voices, and before then only in whispers in the most labyrinthine corridors of military skunkworks facilities, the Colossus Project now enjoys official sanction. Possibly the single greatest military innovation the galaxy will ever see, the Colossus Project comprises the development of a §RPlanet-Killer§! weapons platform as well as a Colossus hull configuration to carry it. The Colossus vessels will likely require an escort as the projected demands of a Planet-Killer weapon preclude any other armament.\n\nNevertheless, the Colossus, once developed, promises to be perhaps the single most destructive force in the galaxy.
apoc.100.desc.pacif: With deterrence theory once again in vogue among leading political scientists on [Root.Capital.GetName], the Colossus Project is presented as the ultimate deterrent; a weapon to surpass even the Titan ship class. While the proposed Colossus ships could carry payloads capable of complete planetary annihilation, we will deploy them using a less violent - but nevertheless terrifyingly permanent - method of conflict resolution.\n\nIf a hypothetical enemy will not cease their aggression toward us or our allies, we must simply §Rmake them§!.
apoc.100.desc.phobe: The Colossus Project is being hailed as the single most important advancement in the ongoing struggle against the wretched aliens that plague the galaxy. As designed, a Colossus ship is a gargantuan, heavily armored frame fitted with a lone §RPlanet-Killer§!-class weapon. Its ability to simply wipe the galaxy clean of planets that will not submit to us will certainly prove invaluable, as the xeno threat is far from over.
apoc.100.desc.purif: By sword and flame shall heretical worlds burn, and with their ashes shall the galaxy be salted.
apoc.100.desc.termi: Atmospheres, biotopes, gravity - while frequently convenient - are only truly needed by the detestable meatbags.\n\nKill the planet, kill the organic.
apoc.100.name: Colossus Project
apoc.11.desc: In what can only be described as a triumph of science and engineering, we have finished construction of our first operational Gateway in the [gateway_system.GetName] system! The device has formed a stable subspace conduit and established a successful link with the rest of the galaxy's Gateway network.
apoc.11.name: Gateway Constructed
apoc.110.desc: Leading scientists across all conceivable fields have at last finalized their proposals for the §RPlanet-Killer§!-class weapon that will arm our first Colossus-type ships. We may select one proposal to develop alongside the final stages of the Colossus Project.
apoc.110.desc.hive: We have explored myriad possibilities, and it is now clear to us that we can develop a suitable §RPlanet-Killer§!-class weapon for our very first Colossus-type vessels. While other avenues can be pursued later, we can only spare the attention to develop one such weapon alongside the final stages of the Colossus Project.
apoc.110.desc.machine: Spare processing cycles have been estimated and deemed sufficient to develop one (1) §RPlanet-Killer§!-class weapon to coincide with completion of §GColossus Project§!.\n\nPrioritization needed.
apoc.110.name: The Gun Pointed at the Head of the Universe
apoc.12.desc: Power has been restored to the derelict Gateway that was found in the §H[gateway_system.GetName]§! system. It has been connected to the rest of the Gateway network and is now fully operational.
apoc.120.desc.hive: The Colossus configuration has fully formed in our mind, ready to be assembled. And, with some unease, we realize that the §R[Root.Get1stPlanetKiller]§! nightmare can also be made manifest.
apoc.120.desc.machine:
Colossus Project completed.

New hull configuration available:
<<§GColossus§!>>

New weapon component available:
<<§R[Root.Get1stPlanetKiller]§!>>
apoc.120.name: Colossus Project Completed
apoc.13.desc: Construction has concluded on the new Gateway in the §H[gateway_system.GetName]§! system. A stable subspace connection to the rest of the Gateway network has been established, and it is now fully operational.
apoc.130.desc: Word has reached us that the [From.GetName] has developed specifications for a Colossus-type hull configuration, a weapon platform potentially capable of complete planetary destruction.
apoc.130.name: [From.GetName] Completes Colossus Project
apoc.14.desc: The deep space construction site for the planned Gateway in the §H[gateway_system.GetName]§! system is now in place. Once we have the necessary resources, construction of the actual Gateway may commence at any time.
apoc.14.name: Gateway Site Ready
apoc.3.b.desc:
We have encountered another abandoned Gateway, this time near §H[gateway_system.GetName]§!. It appears to have been built entirely by microscopic §HNanites§! of an unknown design.

Unlike the previous structure, this Gateway has been significantly altered since its initial construction. Its connection to the rest of the network has been severed - instead, the only valid destination is an uncharted group of stars just beyond our galaxy that has been designated the §HL-Cluster§! by our astronomers.

Although the Gateway emits a faint power signature, it has been deliberately locked into some kind of maintenance loop that prevents its activation. Until we find some way of aborting this process, the L-Cluster will remain beyond our reach.
apoc.3.desc:
We have located what we believe could be an ancient subspace Gateway near §H[gateway_system.GetName]§!. It appears to have been part of a galaxy-wide network of similar stations which, when operational, allowed for near-instantaneous travel from one part of the galaxy to another.

At some point after its initial construction its connection to the rest of the network was severed. It now offers only one valid destination - an uncharted group of stars just beyond our galaxy that our astronomers have designated the §HL-Cluster§!. Even more intriguing, the Gateway was built entirely by microscopic §HNanites§! of an unknown design.

Although the Gateway emits a faint power signature, it has been deliberately locked into some kind of maintenance loop that prevents its activation. Until we find some way of aborting this process, the L-Cluster will remain beyond our reach.
apoc.5.a: If it could somehow be stabilized...
apoc.5.desc: We have detected what appears to be a naturally occurring subspace phenomenon on the edge of the §H[wormhole_system.GetName]§! system! A rift in the very fabric of space-time has formed here, creating a "§Hwormhole§!" that, our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] speculate, may provide a conduit through subspace to another wormhole located somewhere else in our galaxy.\n\nDepending on where the second wormhole is located, this could potentially allow ships to travel from one end of the galaxy to the other in a matter of days. Unfortunately, this wormhole, like the vast majority of its kind, is inherently unstable. Any vessels foolish enough to pass through it would be ripped apart in seconds.
apoc.5.name: Natural Wormhole
aquatic.1.A: It shall be a home like no other.
aquatic_events.250.desc: Following our successes in establishing communications with a number of alien species, one of our leading [This.Owner.GetLinguists] has brought forth a radical proposal. Though past efforts to communicate with the Sky Dragon have failed miserably, [needed_name.GetSheHe] argue[needed_name.GetSXX] that now is the time to make another attempt.\n\nAccording to our earliest histories, there was a fabled Accord between [This.Owner.Species.GetName] and Dragon, after which direct conflict ceased.
