colony.53.name: [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleUpper] Aliens
colony.54.desc: The subterranean aliens on [Root.GetName] have emerged on the surface! Large armies equipped with primitive yet lethal projectile weapons are spilling from the tunnels, and their vanguard has already begun an assault on our settlements.\n\nOur security forces are responding, but we may need to send reinforcements!
colony.54.desc.subterranean: The magma-dwelling aliens on [Root.GetName] have emerged into our caverns! Large armies equipped with primitive yet lethal projectile weapons are spilling from the tunnels, and their vanguard has already begun an assault on our settlements.\n\nOur security forces are responding, but we may need to send reinforcements!
colony.54.name: [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleUpper] Invasion!
colony.56.a: We need to solve this problem for good.
colony.56.desc: Our forces have managed to drive the subterranean aliens on [From.From.GetName] back into their underground lairs, and they are contained for the moment. This is a temporary solution, however, and it is only a matter of time before they break out onto the surface again.\n\nWe need to strike at them below ground, and our strategists have devised a new attack plan. It has been added to the Situation Log.
colony.56.desc.subterranean: Our forces have managed to drive the mantle-dwelling aliens on [From.From.GetName] back into their magma lairs, and they are contained for the moment. This is a temporary solution, however - it is only a matter of time before they break out into our caverns again.\n\nWe need to strike at them below ground, and our strategists have devised a new attack plan. It has been added to the Situation Log.
colony.56.name: Victory on [From.From.GetName]!
colony.57.desc: Our forces have been decimated on [From.From.GetName], and the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens have taken full control over all of our settlements! They are using one of our own satellites to send a message to us.
colony.57.name: Defeat on [From.From.GetName]!
colony.58.desc: Surface creatures! Our glorious armies have bested you in battle, and the spoils of your cities are now ours to do with as we please. We have learned much from your machines, and our weapons are now more powerful than ever.\n\nDo not approach this world again!
colony.58.desc.subterranean: Crust-hugging creatures! Our glorious armies have bested you in battle, and the spoils of your cities are now ours to do with as we please. We have learned much from your machines, and our weapons are now more powerful than ever.\n\nDo not approach this world again!
colony.59.a: Let us see what they have to say.
colony.59.desc: The subterranean aliens on [From.From.GetName] have emerged on the surface! Their excursion appears limited to small bands of explorers and traders. They may be willing to co-exist peacefully with our colonists, and perhaps even engage in trade. We have been contacted by one of their representatives.
colony.59.desc.subterranean: The magma-dwelling aliens on [From.From.GetName] have emerged into our caverns! Their excursion appears limited to small bands of explorers and traders. They may be willing to co-exist peacefully with our colonists, and perhaps even engage in trade. We have been contacted by one of their representatives.
colony.59.name: Aliens Surface
colony.6.desc: We have discovered several significant mineral deposits that had previously been obscured by the roving forests on [Root.GetName]. Now that the trees have been reduced to ashes, the deposits are easy to access.
colony.6.name: Mineral Deposits
colony.60.a: We need to drive them back!
colony.60.desc: The subterranean aliens on [Root.GetName] have marshaled enough forces in their underground empire to launch another invasion of the surface! Once again their frenzied armies are pouring out of freshly dug tunnels to challenge us.
colony.61.desc: Grave news from [Root.GetName]! The [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens we have been fighting there somehow managed to collapse the ground under an entire army that was stationed near one of their tunnel entrances.\n\nThe few soldiers that survived the fall were quickly butchered by the aliens before they could be reached by the rest of our forces.
colony.61.name: Collapse
colony.62.desc: The aliens living below our colony on [Root.GetName] have been sending out small raiding parties from their tunnels at night. Their attacks have destroyed one of the colony's major installations, and before our forces could respond the raiders had vanished underground.
colony.62.name: Raiding Parties
colony.63.a: These murders will not go unanswered.
colony.63.desc: There has been another attack on [Root.GetName]! The [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens emerged from new tunnels in the middle of one of our major settlements. They overwhelmed the local defenses and butchered our colonists. A few screaming survivors were dragged underground by the aliens when they retreated back into their tunnels.
colony.63.name: Surface Attack
colony.64.a: Yes. Put them out of their misery.
colony.64.desc: Our forces on [Root.GetName] are still mapping the tunnel network below our colony. They have come upon a large city belonging to the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens that managed to isolate itself from the rest of their underground empire before we flooded it with nerve gas. There are millions of frightened aliens in the city. Should our engineers collapse the cavern to finish the job?
colony.64.name: Survivor Pocket
colony.65.desc: We have finished clearing out the nerve gas and the dead alien bodies from the tunnel network on [Root.GetName]. It should now be safe for our colonists to move in. The primitive cities the aliens left behind will be demolished, of course, and replaced with our own advanced architecture.
colony.66.desc: Prospectors have ventured into some of the deeper tunnels that once belonged to the now dead subterranean aliens on [Root.GetName]. They have finally discovered the long-rumored gold mines where it was believed the underground alien empire acquired its large reserve of precious metals.
colony.66.desc.subterranean: Prospectors have ventured into some of the deeper tunnels that once belonged to the now dead magma-dwellers on [Root.GetName]. They have finally discovered the long-rumored gold mines where it was believed the underground alien empire acquired its large reserve of precious metals.
colony.66.name: Gold!
colony.67.desc: Scout units exploring the tunnel network on [Root.GetName] have entered the royal palace in what was once the capital city of the underground alien empire. The corpse of what passed for their emperor is still perched on a massive throne in the main chamber.\n\nAfter using explosive charges to breach the palace treasury, our scouts found it filled with gold and strange alien art. The art will be shipped back to museums on [From.Owner.Capital.GetName], and the sale of the gold should provide a nice boost to our state budget.
colony.67.name: Treasury
colony.68.desc: [Root.GetName] has been racked by another wave of earthquakes recently. It seems that some of the deeper parts of the underground tunnel network has collapsed without the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens to maintain it. Many of our settlements have suffered damage.
colony.68.name: Earthquakes on [Root.GetName]
colony.69.a: Of course. We will help however we can.
colony.69.b: They'll have to fend for themselves.
colony.69.desc: We have been approached by a delegation from the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens on [Root.GetName]. It seems their empire has fallen on hard times recently, and they are facing the threat of a famine. They are pleading with us to provide whatever assistance we can.
colony.69.name: Famine
colony.7.desc: We have discovered a significant deposit of precious metals that had previously been obscured by the roving forests on [Root.GetName]. Now that the trees have been reduced to ashes, the deposit is easy to access.
colony.7.name: Precious Metal Deposit
colony.70.desc: As a gift to celebrate the friendship between our two civilizations, a caravan from the subterranean aliens on [Root.GetName] has brought a large quantity of gemstones to the surface. Stones such as these are apparently mined by their empire deep underground, as close to the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s core as they dare to venture.
colony.70.desc.subterranean: As a gift to celebrate the friendship between our two civilizations, a caravan from the magma-dwellers on [Root.GetName] has brought a large quantity of gemstones to our caverns. Stones such as these are apparently mined deep underground, as close to the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s core as their civilization dares to venture.
colony.70.name: Gift
colony.71.a: Let them join our colony if that is their wish.
colony.71.b: We can't afford a political incident. Send them back.
colony.71.desc: A large group of refugees from the underground alien empire on [Root.GetName] recently streamed out of their tunnels onto the surface, chased by a small army. They are apparently part of some sort of religious minority; they claim to be fleeing persecution.\n\nIf we let them join our colonists on the surface, it will no doubt anger the rulers of the empire they fled from. However, if we let the pursuing army take them back underground, they will likely face execution.
colony.71.desc.subterranean: A large group of refugees from the magma-dweller empire on [Root.GetName] recently streamed out of their tunnels into our caverns, chased by a small army. They are apparently part of some sort of religious minority; they claim to be fleeing persecution.\n\nIf we let them join our colonists in the upper caverns, it will no doubt anger the rulers of the empire they are fleeing from. However, if we let the pursuing army take them back underground, they will likely face execution.
colony.71.name: [root.Owner.GetSubMantleUpper] Refugees
colony.72.desc: Several xeno anthropologists from [Root.Owner.Capital.GetName] have returned to the surface of [Root.GetName] after spending a great deal of time living among the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens native to that world. They have learned much about their ancient ways and customs, which will no doubt benefit our society research.
colony.72.name: Xeno Anthropologists
colony.73.desc: There has been a wave of earthquakes on [Root.GetName] recently, and buildings in several of our settlements have collapsed with many fatalities as a result. The [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] alien empire is excavating a new cavern deep underground where they plan to build a new city, and this appears to be the source of the earthquakes.
colony.74.a: Arming savages with modern weapons would be a bad idea.
colony.74.b: They are our friends. Share what we can.
colony.74.desc: After seeing the advanced weapons that our security forces are equipped with, several generals from the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] alien empire on [Root.GetName] have come forward requesting that we share some of our military technology.\n\nOur own officers are hesitant to do this, as it would make the aliens more difficult to defeat in battle should it ever come to that. If we refuse the request, however, the aliens are certain to view it as an insult.
colony.74.name: Request for Technology
colony.75.desc: Trade with the [Root.Owner.GetSubMantleLower] aliens on [Root.GetName] has dried up as of late, with their caravans showing up more and more seldom. Today we received a message from a representative of their military. They don't seem very pleased.
colony.75.name: Message Delivered
colony.76.desc: Surfacer. We tried to be good neighbors, but it has become clear that you have no intention of treating us with the respect our glorious civilization deserves.\n\nOur emperor has thus decreed that we must claim this entire world for ourselves, as is our right. We shall drive you back to the stars from whence you came!
colony.76.desc.subterranean: Crust-hugger. We tried to be good neighbors, but it has become clear that you have no intention of treating us with the respect our glorious civilization deserves.\n\nOur emperor has thus decreed that we must claim this entire world for ourselves, as is our right. We shall drive you back to the stars from whence you came!
colony.76.name: Message
colony.8.desc: It would appear the migrating forests we exterminated on [Root.GetName] played a more vital role in the [Root.GetPlanetMoon]'s ecology than previously thought. The wildfires we started and the absence of the forests have led to the extinction of several local species, resulting in a domino effect that has claimed several species of predators as well.\n\nEfforts are ongoing to at least partly restore the fragile ecological balance by introducing new flora and fauna from other worlds, but it is a difficult process that will take time.
colony.8.name: Ecological Damage
colony.8001.desc: Reports from our colony on [Planet.GetName] claims that there's been an increase in 'feral behavior'. Apparently parts of the population has expressed hitherto unprecedented levels of lust and aggression, and no one knows why.
colony.8001.name: Feral Behavior
colony.8002.a: This is getting out of hand.
colony.8002.desc: The feral behavior on [Planet.GetName] shows no signs of stopping anytime soon. In fact, it has risen since the last report. Promiscuous and violent acts happen all the time, and a large part of the population seems to be affected.
colony.8002.name: Violence on the Rise
colony.8003.desc: The situation on [Planet.GetName] has spiraled out of control. A staggering number of inhabitants are now infected with whatever is causing this feral deluge, and the colony has started to break down because of it. Something needs to be done, or [Planet.GetName] will be lost.
colony.8003.name: This is Madness!
colony.8004.desc:
The investigation of the strange and wild behavior currently besetting [Planet.GetName] has been completed. In the vast network of cave tunnels that permeates the planet's crust an enigmatic fungus has been found. It grows all over the caves - floor, walls, ceiling - and stretches out for thousands of miles.

The fungus frequently releases spores that are vented out of the caves - for what purpose has not been established, but we know for certain that it causes primitive behavior in our species, releasing primal urges within.

We can try to find a useful application of this phenomenon, or we can exterminate the fungus altogether.
colony.8004.name: Savage Spores
colony.8005.desc: Industrial facilities have been built over the outlets for the fungus-infested cave systems. Apart from filtering and regulating the spread of spores, these plants can also convert any excess spore clouds into useful §Hexotic gases§!.\n\nThe population growth is increased as the somewhat randy inhabitants of [Planet.GetName] satisfy their urges more frequently, which unfortunately also means that the level of violence and conflict is somewhat higher on [Planet.GetName].
colony.8005.name: Cloud and Strife
colony.8006.desc: The project to incinerate all Cave Mushrooms have now been completed and the primal urge-inducing fungus has been exterminated.\n\nAs luck would have it, several of the burned-out caves turned out to have rich mineral veins, which can now be exploited further.
colony.8006.name: The Cleansing Flames
colony.9.desc: Continued interaction between our colonists and the wandering forests on [Root.GetName] has revealed that the trees are in possession of some form of rudimentary communal intelligence. They seem to have adapted to our presence, and now go out of their way to avoid damaging the property of our colonists even without the use of the insect pheromone. Spirits among the colonists have risen.
colony.9.name: Forest Adaptation
colony.9000.desc: Our colony on [Root.GetName] has encountered an odd situation: we have apparently settled on the back of a gargantuan amphibian reptile, whose bony shell is formed of various exotic minerals. Most of what we thought were local islands have turned out to be these creatures; our colonists have begun to refer to them as '§YNemmas§!'.\n\nThey seem harmless enough, and as long as we don't dig too deep into their shell, they should barely notice us.
colony.9000.name: Unsteady Ground
colony.9005.desc:
As our colony at [Root.GetName] has been flourishing, the adolescents of this new world have sought to create entertainment for themselves - as youths are wont to do. Some groups have made a game of sneaking up as close as they dare to their local Nemma's head.

Unfortunately, this daring activity has led to tragedy: after startling the beast, several young [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] fell off the neck of the massive creature, resulting in injuries and one fatality.

Distraught colonists are now asking for something to be done about these "brutish behemoths."
colony.9005.desc.gestalt: While our [Root.GetName] colony has been flourishing, it has become apparent that Nemmas have a strong aversion to our drones venturing near their head. This became starkly apparent when one such beast flinched and dislodged several [Root.Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] from its neck, causing severe damage.\n\nOur progress will be restrained unless we do something to handle these behemoths.
colony.9005.name: A Daring Discovery
colony.9010.a: Breed more Nemmas and safeguard them for more living space.
colony.9010.b: Enslave the Nemmas so that they become deferential and compliant.
colony.9010.c: Enough! Sedate the Nemmas, and start drilling their shells.
colony.9010.desc: Having tasked our best biologists and engineers with devising potential solutions for the Nemma dilemma on [Root.GetName], several proposals are now ready to be presented.\n\nWe've considered everything from the most rational to the most extreme of ideas. The urgency of this situation demands we must skip straight to live field tests.
colony.9010.name: Nemma Taskforce
colony.9015.desc: After initial trials with the adult specimen, our zoologists have set up a Nemma breeding system on [Root.GetName] in the hopes of introducing more giant Nemmas to our oceans. The breeders warn that this cannot continue indefinitely, and that the planet can only support three, perhaps four more Nemmas. The estimated time until we have our next Nemma should be about §Yten years§!.
colony.9015.name: Expand the Archipelago
colony.9020.desc: Our breeding program on [Root.GetName] bears fruit as we add another Nemma to our ranks! This juvenile has quickly acclimated to our presence, and we have found it a stable habitat. The Nemma should now be ready to bear our industry.
colony.9020.desc.full: $colony.9020.desc$\n\nThis will, however, have to be the last Nemma added to this world, as their habitat has reached capacity. Our Nemma wranglers will have to refocus their efforts not on breeding more Nemmas, but instead on maintaining what they already have created.
colony.9020.name: The Miracle of Life
colony.9025.desc: Sadly the latest effort to add another Nemma to [Root.GetName] has failed; we could find no habitat spacious enough for such a massive beast to thrive. The [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] are not dismayed, however, and promise better results in the future.
colony.9025.name: Overpopulation
colony.9030.a: Excellent work, now our true work can begin.
colony.9030.desc: Our xeno-bioengineering [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] have curtailed the Nemma menace! Thanks to our superb efforts, the creatures are now subservient to us.\n\nThe Nemmas have been granted renewed purpose as superlative beasts of burden. Their colossal bulk allows them to carry immense quantities of materiel, guided down optimal routes by way of their cybernetic implants. Our colonization effort has accelerated accordingly.
colony.9030.name: Enforced Obedience
colony.9035.b: Arrest the instigators and put them on waste disposal duty.
colony.9035.desc: Today riots broke out on [Root.GetName] as parts of the population have risen in protest against our treatment of the Nemmas. The protestors formed a picket line around the head of the Nemma on which the colony's capital lies. The protestors demanded that we immediately set all the Nemmas free, working to conserve their species rather than enslave them.\n\nThe movement has quickly spread to sites around the other Nemmas - however, counter-protests have formed in favor of our existing programs, escalating public tension and risking outbursts of violence.
colony.9035.name: Nemma Huggers
colony.9040.desc: Our engineers and biochemists have outdone themselves. Newly developed drugs and extremely precise drills will allow us to harvest the minerals by drilling into the hard crystalline shell of these Nemmas, as well as allowing us to collect biomatter from beneath without jeopardizing our infrastructure. If only all our colonies could yield such bounties.
colony.9040.name: Exploiting the Shells
colony.9045.a: The only way to handle such mindless beasts.
colony.9045.desc: The purging of the Nemmas has been completed - all very systematically, so as not to pollute the oceans or otherwise endanger our infrastructure. Soon we can turn our attention to the task of harvesting their remains, and establishing a more permanent and enduring colony on [Root.GetName]. First, however, we need to store all the leftovers.
colony.9045.name: Exterminate the Perpetual Reptiles
colony.9050.desc: Geological surveys on [Root.GetName] have revealed that the planet is richer in minerals than we thought. After calibrating our sensors to penetrate deeper into the ground, we have discovered several promising mining sites. Should we direct additional resources to probing efforts, we might yet uncover deeper veins of useful ore.
colony.9050.name: Unexpected Mineral Seams
colony.9055.desc: Probing the underground of [Root.GetName] is a tedious process: our scanners do not react well to the ground composition, and shifts in the geological layers mean that we have to recalibrate them every time. Still, we have discovered more exploitable veins of high quality ore. Their depths makes the logistics of the mining operation more complex than usual, but it will take more than that to stop us. There is no assurance that additional probing operations will lead us to more mineral veins.
colony.9055.name: Deep Veins
colony.9060.desc: The latest prospecting efforts on [Root.GetName] were inconclusive. Whatever minerals we could detect were buried too deep, in too small quantities, and through unstable ground. The projected costs of exploiting these veins would be higher than the profits. Despite this, our previous findings represents an enormous source of resources that should keep us busy for decades if not centuries.
colony.9060.name: Too Little, Too Deep
colony.9065.desc: No matter how deep the minerals on [Root.GetName] are hidden, we will find and extract them. It is what we do. Others might give up when confronted with unstable grounds, unfathomable depths or the logistics of maintaining transport tunnels, but we do not. The underground is our home, and if we know where to look, it will provide. The lower we go, the higher the quality and quantity of the ore. Our latest samples even hinted at the presence of rare crystals deeper.
colony.9065.name: More Ore
colony.9070.a: These probing works are too expensive.
colony.9070.b: Then a digging we shall go.
colony.9070.desc: A new depth has been reached by our surveying expeditions on [Root.GetName]. As predicted, we are encountering clusters of crystals that shine in vivid hues of oranges, yellows, and reds when light passes through them. At times, it looks as if a brazier is illuminating the caves where we find them, casting shifting shadows on the walls. We also made a puzzling observation: it looks as if over the millennia, these crystals are slowly migrating towards the center of the planet. We are confident that there will be more to find if only we dig deeper towards the core.
colony.9070.name: Fiery Crystals
colony.9075.name: The Price of Greed
colony.9080.desc: After a grueling campaign, the crystalline entity dwelling at the heart of a planet has finally been defeated. The final battle took place deep underground, in the cave housing the core of the crystal behemoth, and only after we managed to shatter it did the beast stop fighting. Its various appendages disintegrated, losing cohesion at a molecular level and sprinkling crystal dust across the planet. The innumerable tunnels left in the wake of crystal tentacles are going to help us a lot in our efforts to mine the exceptionally rich minerals composing this world. As for the origin of the entity itself, we are left with many questions, but we might have just gained some insight on the way that spacefaring crystalline entities are created.
colony.9080.name: Crystalline Entity Defeated
colony.9085.desc: Our mining operations on [Root.GetName] have encountered unexpected difficulties. Ranging from mild tremors to shifting crystal veins, something is going on. Despite all our experience in tunneling, we have no idea what it is. These circumstances make it hard to work in secure conditions, and we have already lost gear, lives and ore in unpredictable accidents and collapses. Perhaps it would be best to halt mining operations under a certain depth?
colony.9085.name: Unusual Happenings
colony.9200.a.desc: Setting up the grid might take some time, and will continue to sip the energy during the exploration of the vault.
colony.9200.desc: During a standard reconnaissance of [Root.GetName], the planetary exploration unit came across a massive door that apparently leads directly into the interior of a mountain range. It appears that the strong magnetic field produced by some sort of cloaking device hid it from our ship's sensors, and the camouflaged entrance remained invisible to the autonomous research probes mapping the surface.\n\nOn the other hand, more specialized tests have shown that delivering a steady stream of energy should make the door operational again, eventually allowing us to open it and see what's inside.
colony.9201.a.desc: Given the scope of this operation, it will take a lot of resources, workforce, and an unknown amount of time to study it thoroughly. Regular updates and reports on their work are somewhat to be expected.
colony.9201.b.desc: We will seal the entrance and demolish this place. Who knows what might lurk inside this vault.
colony.9201.desc: As energy flowed through the circuits, the entrance came online, and with additional tinkering, we quickly discovered how the door worked. Additional topographical research revealed the interior to be a large underground vault. Alien infrastructure covered every square centimeter of the walls - even the huge pillars supporting the ceiling showed faint energy signatures. Given the energy readings and vague similarities to our technology, it appears to be an underground manufacturing facility.
colony.9202.desc: Those far from the vault could feel the ground shake. Those closer could see a large chunk of the mountainside fly off into the air, creating a huge crater filled with rocks, debris, and twisted machinery. A quick guess as to what could have gone wrong led to the conclusion that a chain reaction was set in motion inside the vault when the initial explosion breached the door.\n\nRegardless, a smoking crater is all that is left of the underground vault.
colony.9210.a.desc: We will form a search team, but a lot of citizens already anticipate the worst. We will also double the guards to prevent further incidents.
colony.9210.b.desc: We can't leave them to die! We will make a volunteer squad to look for the missing!
colony.9210.c.desc: It was expected that something like this might have happened. We will try to find the missing workers, but we can't delay our operations - we are ready to pay the price.
colony.9210.d.desc: Missing units will be replaced with new ones. The research has to continue.
colony.9210.desc: The initial phase of research on [Root.GetName] was largely focused on mapping the entrance. The first room within the vault is a giant hall, stretching deep into the mountain, with several branching corridors pushing even further into the depths. Various ornate plaques decorate stone chiseled pillars, each depicting the alien race that presumably built this place. We can't decipher their language, but the story told by those art pieces are centered on warfare, struggle, and grandiose projects.\n\nMore disturbing is the loss of an entire construction unit; after reporting the presence of strange sounds in the dark, the unit simply vanished. The situation is in danger of slipping out of control and calls for more decisive action.
colony.9211.desc: One of our security teams reports that the missing workers have been found. It turns out that this vault still has operational traps and devices that were programmed to trap unwanted visitors within "boxes" comprised of dislocated and moving walls.\n\nThe unfortunate workers were all killed within the trap. Our citizenry is furious at the result, but at least now we know what to look for.
colony.9212.desc: Given the enormous search team, it didn't take long to find the missing workers. The last of them were discovered trapped in a square prison-like structure made of articulated and self-moving walls. It appears that the security systems within the vault are still operational. Given this, we will be more prepared to counter such contraptions in the future. Nonetheless, the population is angry that the workers were not provided with proper safety measures in the first place.
colony.9213.desc: The missing workers were found in a grotesque contraption that imprisoned them between four movable walls. Unfortunately, these individuals are no longer of any use to the empire, but at least their sacrifice revealed the existence of the trap. The work now continues undisturbed, and the population working on the site feels some relief, knowing that they should be safe - for now.
colony.9214.desc: The missing drones were found in an ingenious contraption of moving walls that linked together to create enclosed prison spaces. Unfortunately, all of our drones are damaged beyond use. From now on, our surveying drones will use this knowledge to neutralize traps of this kind. Work continues without any further disturbances.
colony.9220.a.desc: It's just a useless piece of old art, with no real value.
colony.9220.b.desc: Some of our craftsmen are astonished by the work created by those aliens. They find a hint of old beauty and harmony in their art.
colony.9220.c.desc: Our people find the stonework to be of absolutely extraordinary quality, which is very soothing to find in such an unfamiliar place.
colony.9220.d.desc: This place looks almost like the work made by our greatest stonemasons and artificers. Is this a mere coincidence?
colony.9220.desc: We delved into the corridors at [Root.GetName] and discovered a large hall, which is strangely devoid of the pipe machines covering every other hallway and wall. It looks like whoever built this place took special care of it - there are many statues here in excellent condition, depicting bipedal individuals. With some traces of detail they have mostly a uniform appearance. Unfortunately, there is no evidence of what this hall was, other than some monumental tribute to probably historical figures.
colony.9230.desc: Our seismographs have detected an impending earthquake on [Root.GetName]. Most of the workers have found safety, but one group is in a remote hall that could be at risk of collapse. They reported two distinct, ancient machines there - one being a bulky contraption connected to the ground, and the other attached to the walls via a series of pipes. We can't say if they are anything important for the facility. The workers have estimated that may be possible to use one of those machines to reinforce the ceiling and walls against the quake.
colony.9231.desc: Our workers managed to disassemble the machinery and have successfully bolstered the strength of the supports and ceiling. However, this effort exposed extensive piping in the walls, from which a hissing noise escapes. Right now, it's impossible to assess the potential losses.
colony.9232.desc: Our workers managed to disassemble the machinery and used it with success to bolster the strength of the old supports and the ceiling - but what was the cost really? Removing the bulky machine resulted in a gaping hole in the ground leading deeper inside the machinery. Potential losses to this action are, for now, completely unknown.
colony.9233.desc: Our workers were able to properly assess the situation and managed to repair and strengthen the supports without destroying the ancient machinery.
colony.9234.desc: Gathering the sense impressions of various drones, a better solution was found: the hall has been strengthened to a safe degree at the cost of a few menial drones.
colony.9240.a.desc: We will try to pry open the doors with power tools and heavy machinery. With some luck, we will be inside with no further problems.
colony.9240.b.desc: Sometimes the violent approach is the best approach. Set explosives and be done with it.
colony.9240.c.desc: Let's not be hasty. We encountered various traps before. Sometimes it's better not to rush with obvious solutions.
colony.9240.d.desc: We are skilled in overcoming problems with unusual solutions, so we might be able to find other way inside.
colony.9240.desc: Our exploration on [Root.GetName] finally yielded some insights. Our first assessment turned out to be correct. The vault is in fact a giant foundry. Further analysis of the alien language reveals that it was referred to as a King-Forge. However, the Forge was never operational - its builders apparently lacked the technology to see the project through to completion.\n\nIt should be possible for us to finish their work as long as we can get into the heart of the foundry. Although the way is blocked by heavy doors, our engineers insist they can be overcome. However, as the doors don't have any obvious locking or opening mechanisms, a certain application of force will be required before we can proceed.
colony.9240.e.desc: Our drones will cut through the doors with ease. It will take some time, but we have all the time in the cosmos.
colony.9241.desc: After forcing the doors, the machinery covering the walls started to leak hazardous gas. Unfortunately, this happened too quickly, and the result was further casualties. The entire facility needed to be evacuated, and will have to be left for some time before we can safely reenter.
colony.9242.desc: Opening the door with explosives was easy, but what we didn't anticipate was the gas that poured into the hallway after the explosion. It turned out that the gas was highly flammable and destroyed some of the ever-present machinery. Fortunately, there was no one in the blast zone, so there were no casualties.
colony.9243.desc: Whether by luck or divine intervention, the same door that blocked the way forward responded to our morning rituals: a faint harmonic resonance was detected, a resonance we were eventually able to manipulate. The correct set of gestures made in front of a small marking that concealed the lens of a camera ensured that we gained unobstructed entry.
colony.9244.desc: After additional research, we quickly recognized something in the door that served as a security camera or scanner. Hacking into it was a more difficult task, but we were able to decipher its programming and basic functions - thus gaining access to the door without further complication.
colony.9245.desc: It appears in drilling through the door, our drones activated some defensive mechanism that unleashed weaponized gas inside the corridor. Fortunately, the Collective was able to take proper precautions, and soon enough the gas had dissipated. The drones have already returned to work.
colony.9250.a.desc: We will plug the machinery into the planetary power grid and fix it.
colony.9250.b.desc: Fixing the machinery is not enough - we need to learn how it works.
colony.9250.c.desc: This foundry will serve the empire and provide us with potential knowledge about its original inhabitants.
colony.9250.d.desc: This foundry will serve the hive and provide us with potential knowledge about its original inhabitants.
colony.9250.desc: The heart of the foundry on [Root.GetName] is a twisted network of pipes, conveyor belts, and what appear to be workstations. A quick survey revealed that power, maintenance, and key systems are missing. There is also reason to believe that our exploration of the vault has had some effect on the internal workings of the foundry. We can try to repair it, though it will be time consuming. Alternatively, we can always set up a scrapyard and dismantle the entire machine.
colony.9250.e.desc: Fixing the machinery is not enough - we need to learn how it works.
colony.9250.f.desc: The scrapyard will begin its slow process of dismantling the machinery.
colony.9251.desc: Energy flows through the hungry machines on [Root.GetName]. With a deafening roar, the pipes began to transport the liquefied minerals, brightening and heating the entire facility. The raw materials were delivered to the workstations where operators can form them into alloys of the desired shape and density. It looks like every part of the foundry was made with just this one purpose in mind. Even the pillars have more to do than support the ceiling.
colony.9260.a.desc: We will rotate the operators before they get sick. An occasional headache might occur.
colony.9260.b.desc: We will issue breaks, allowing the gas to dissipate for safer workplace.
colony.9260.c.desc: Who cares about slaves? We could always give them better clothes, and they will be happy to risk their health.
colony.9260.d.desc: Worker rotation, time regulations, and protections on-site - we must mitigate the hazards without hampering our productivity.
colony.9260.desc: There is some concern that toxic gases are building up in the main chamber of the [Root.GetName] vault. The gas is non-lethal, but it can be hazardous to anything that operates workstations. If we want to make full use of this place, we should put some safety measures in place.
colony.9260.e.desc: Every drone works for the consciousness till they fill its purpose.
colony.9270.a.desc: We will bring the recycling center online.
colony.9270.b.desc: Our recycling patterns are far superior. We could implement them into the machinery.
colony.9270.c.desc: We can repurpose the recycling chamber into a mineral purifying center. It will enhance our production.
colony.9270.desc: The [Root.GetName] foundry has a dedicated recyclable processing chamber that uses post-production waste to increase production efficiency. It might be beneficial for us to get it up and running again.
colony.9280.b.desc: We will increase the production, but also mineral upkeep.
colony.9280.c.desc: We could supplant some part of the mineral intake with organic matter, but it will be impossible to fully implement it.
colony.9280.d.desc: We once ruled a vast empire and had technology beyond comparison. Some recently rediscovered technology could use us to enhance the production capacity of the foundry.
colony.9280.desc: Work on the [Root.GetName] foundry is almost complete, but there are still places where we could improve on the original design and work. It is estimated that by increasing the amount of minerals input, we could increase the production of the alloy.
colony.9290.b.desc: We never really found out what happened to the builders. They seem to have simply disappeared, leaving behind only vague information about themselves. We need to gather everything we can and write it down - preserve it.
colony.9290.c.desc: It's customary for our elites to oversee such enterprise - we should appoint prominent noble to take care of our new foundry.
colony.9290.desc: It's finished! The foundry on [Root.GetName] is fully operational, perhaps not like its original Builders designed it, but it's still a sight to behold, and a more-than-efficient way to produce alloys. All that's left is to reap the rewards of our determination and ingenuity.
colony.9295.a: Leave them alone. They may be toxic!
colony.9295.desc: After a recent rainfall, colonists have noticed metallic puddles appearing on the surface of [Root.GetName]. These puddles have a viscous consistency, like liquid metal.
colony.9295.name: Metallic Puddles
colony.9296.desc: The viscous metallic puddles on [Root.GetName] are growing. Huge swathes of land are now covered in silver slime. They seem to grow following heavy rainfall.
colony.9296.name: Silver Slime
colony.9297.a: Sometimes these things just resolve themselves...
colony.9297.desc: They're gone! The viscous metallic puddles on [Root.GetName] have disappeared. It's as if they've just evaporated. We don't know if or when they'll be back again...
colony.9297.name: Disappearing Puddles
colony.9298.desc: They're back! The viscous metallic puddles on [Root.GetName] have returned. Their nature continues to elude the colonists on [Root.GetName]. We've been handed another opportunity. We should investigate them while we can.
colony.9298.name: Return of the Silver Slime
colony.9299.desc: The viscous metallic puddles on [Root.GetName] are eluding colony scientists. So far their origin is undetermined, and they have been resistant to our probing. Our instruments are struggling to decipher their chemical makeup. We have more tests to run if we want answers.
colony.9299.name: Elusive Viscosity
colony.9300.a: We still have much to learn.
colony.9300.name: Elementary, Dear Leader!
colony.9301.desc: We have gained invaluable insight into the unique weather systems of [Root.GetName]. In addition to expanding our understanding of chemical elements, our recent research has had positive implications for food production.
colony.9301.name: Invaluable Insight
colony.9800.desc: The Dimensional Portal on [Root.GetName] shut itself. When we stabilized the portal, we saw that it led to a dimension consisting solely of a white, formless void interrupted only by random streaks of black noise. The strange phenomenon instantly started to seep into our universe and consumed our dimensional stabilizers, collapsing the gateway.\n\nThe portal, static, and dimensional stabilizers have all winked out of existence simultaneously. Nothing was left behind; not even trace particles. If the portal hadn't been unstable, who knows what kind of disaster might have occurred here.
colony.9800.name: A Dimension of Static
colony.9805.desc: Recently our [Root.GetScientistPlural] working in our primary physics lab on §Y[Root.GetHomeWorldName]§! have noticed strange fluctuations in their work. Our hyperdrive-related tests suffered most from these interferences, yet these interruptions only went on for about a week before stopping entirely. At the same time [From.GetName] noticed fluctuations from the now closed dimensional portal, thankfully the impossible static did not return. Hopefully, nothing will come of this.
colony.9805.name: Disruptions
colony.9810.desc:
Eager and anxious discourse started in the scientific circles of [Root.GetHomeWorldName] today as [cloned_physicist.GetName] published [cloned_physicist.GetHerHis] recent findings of spontaneously appearing negative mass particles close to §Y[Root.Capital.GetStarName]§!.

"These findings could advance our understanding of artificial wormholes and a host of other subjects," proclaims [cloned_physicist.GetName]!

Our Admiralty holds a different view on the subject and suggests we bring our fleets home until the source of this new and untested matter can be determined.
colony.9810.desc.hive:
New observations from physics specialized drone [cloned_physicist.GetName] have been disseminated regarding the recent findings of spontaneously appearing negative mass particles close to §Y[Root.Capital.GetStarName]§!.

"These findings could advance the [Root.GetName] understanding of artificial wormholes and additional related subjects," reports the drone.

The Mind is untrusting of this sudden development and instinctively feels an urge to return some fleets to the spawning system.
colony.9810.desc.robot:
A new report from lead physics unit [cloned_physicist.GetName] was received today. The report included recent findings of the spontaneously appearing negative mass particles close to §Y[Root.Capital.GetStarName]§!.

"These findings could advance the [Root.GetName] understanding of artificial wormholes immensely as well as related subjects," reports science unit [cloned_physicist.GetName].

Threat analysis subroutines suggest bringing fleets home until the source of this new and untested material can be determined.
colony.9810.name: Negative Mass
colony.9815.desc: The greatest minds of the [Root.GetName] gathered today to listen to [cloned_physicist.GetName]'s latest ideas for using the negative mass particles, only to be interrupted. Emergency sirens screeched in every observatory and space station across the system as §Y[Root.GetHomeWorldName]§! got a new fixture in the night sky. A rip in space the size of our star stretches over horizons while a small fleet of fighters pours through the tear.
colony.9815.desc.hive: Additional drones had been deployed to study [cloned_physicist.GetName]'s latest findings and the use of the negative mass particles only to be interrupted. Emergency sirens screeched in every observatory and space station across the system as §Y[Root.GetHomeWorldName]§! got a new fixture in the night sky. A rip in space the size of our star stretches over the sky as a small fleet of fighters pours out of the tear.
colony.9815.desc.robot: Additional science units had been deployed to study [cloned_physicist.GetName]'s latest findings and the use of the negative mass particles only to be interrupted. Emergency sirens screeched in every observatory and space station across the system as §Y[Root.GetHomeWorldName]§! got a new fixture in the night sky. A rip in space the size of our star stretches over the sky as a small fleet of fighters pours out of the tear.
colony.9815.name: The Night the Sky Split
colony.9820.desc: As the last corvette falls, an ensign manning the sensors of our starbase reports something curious. These ships are very similar to outdated vessels that the [Root.GetName] stopped using years ago. The ships are lacking FTL drives and are equipped with obsolete weaponry. While the report is coming in, a communication request originating from the strange tear reverberates throughout the system. It's using our highest clearance codes... from 10 years ago.
colony.9820.desc.hive: As the last corvette falls, a drone manning the sensors reports something curious. These ships are very similar to outdated vessels that the [Root.GetName] stopped using years ago. The ships are lacking FTL drives and are equipped with obsolete weaponry. While the report is coming in, a communication request originating from the strange tear reverberates throughout the system. It's something this Mind is unfamiliar with, another [Root.GetSpeciesName] intelligence.
colony.9820.desc.robot: As the last corvette is rendered inoperable, observation analysis subroutines report something abnormal. The invader ships are similar to outdated vessels that the [Root.GetName] stopped producing years ago. Additionally, the ships lack FTL drives and are equipped with obsolete weaponry. While the report is coming in, a communication request originating from the strange tear reverberates throughout the system. It's using our most complex handshaking protocols... from 10 years ago.
colony.9820.name: An Old Code
colony.9821.b: Why do you seem to be lacking FTL capabilities?
colony.9821.c: Enough talk. What do you want?
colony.9821.desc: As the comms screen flickers on, what looks to be the most exhausted, elated, and simultaneously terrified [Root.GetSpeciesName] imaginable appears. They look familiar, a dead ringer for [cloned_physicist.GetName] if [cloned_physicist.GetHeShe] had aged 20 years. §B"Ah... hello [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Alpha, this is [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Beta"§! they stop to gather themselves. §B"I, uh, we... We are terribly sorry for what just transpired. You have to understand, that was a rogue and defunct element of our world's defense collective thinking they could seize [Root.GetHomeWorldName] by force. I know the words might sound empty, but please believe me when I say that we have no ill intention towards you."§!
colony.9821.desc.hive: As the comms screen flickers on the other Mind communication drone has an identical structure as [cloned_physicist.GetName]. Curious. §B"Greetings [Root.GetName]-Alpha and apologies. The drones that attacked you were deviants left to their own devices too long. [Root.GetName]-Beta appreciates that you exterminated them. We desire no more negative interactions and want to propose something beneficial for both our minds."§!
colony.9821.desc.robot: As the comms screen flickers on, an identification code is sent through. §RChecksum error:§! This is [cloned_physicist.GetName]s unique ID! \n§B"Greetings [Root.GetName]-Alpha and apologies: Previous hostile action was caused by a redundant and deprecated military branch of [Root.GetName]-Beta systems. It has since been dealt with and deleted. Statement: We intend no further hostile interactions."§!
colony.9821.name: A Trans-Dimensional Call
colony.9822.a: We must confer with our experts.
colony.9822.a.hive: This Mind needs to reflect on this request.
colony.9822.desc: §BOur universe is doomed. There is no way to get around that. We have been building giant transport ships for this day and implore you to let us send over refugees. Only our brightest and most capable leaders will fit on these ships. Please save my-§! §YOUR§! §Bcivilization.§!
colony.9822.desc.hive: §B[Root.GetName]-Beta's universe is doomed. There is no way to get around that. We have been building giant transport ships for this very day and would offer any drones we could send.\nAdditionally we wish to merge hiveminds. While identical at first this collective has had experiences and insights we don't want to lose. Please let us live on.§!
colony.9822.desc.robot: §BTransportation ships have been built. Request to send over [Root.GetName]-Beta units to preserve resources and databanks. We do not wish to end our exploration of the universe here.§!
colony.9840.a.tooltip: We cannot spare the resources for such an undertaking, but we won't let an opportunity like this go to waste.
colony.9840.b.tooltip: These fools have left themselves defenseless!
colony.9840.d.tooltip: Start a difficult project to save [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta.
colony.9840.desc: A summit of the top minds from every field gathered on §Y[Root.GetName]§! to discuss the fate of our dimensional twins. Harsh and difficult debates were had throughout [Root.GetHomeWorldName]. Some suggested a hands-off approach. Studying the end of a universe could be very insightful. There was talk about granting [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Beta's request to evacuate as much of the planet as possible while some mentioned how easy it would be to take whatever precious resources and energy stores the planet had left.\n\nJust as the summit was winding down, [cloned_physicist.GetName] took center stage and declared that [cloned_physicist.GetHeShe] believed that using the new technologies brought from the beta universe, there was a chance to bring the entirety of [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta into our reality.
colony.9840.desc.hive:
As the full might of [Root.GetSpeciesName]'s intelligence was put on the task of deciding the fate of [Root.GetName]-Beta 4 main potential solutions were proposed.

1: Study collapse of the Beta universe.
2: Enter the gateway and acquire all relevant stockpiles of minerals and energy.
3: Accept [Root.GetName]-Beta request and subsume the other Mind.
4: Attempt to use highly experimental Beta science and technology to bring [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta into Alpha reality merging Minds.
colony.9840.desc.robot:
Every supercomputer under the control of [Root.GetName] was put on calculating the most optimal solution to the current dilemma regarding [Root.GetName]-Beta. In the end, 4 potential options were declared viable.

1: Study collapse of Beta universe.
2: Enter gateway and acquire all relevant stockpiles of minerals and energy.
3: Allow science unit: [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Beta's proposal.
4: Attempt to use highly experimental Beta science and technology to bring [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta into Alpha reality.
colony.9840.name: The Summit
colony.9850.desc: A formless static covers a large swath of §B[Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta's§! sky and is closing in rapidly as [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Alpha and Beta, working side by side, finish their arduous task. The negative mass stabilizers activate, and the tear between worlds moves over [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta just as the static would smother it. The rift winks out moments later, and negative mass stops appearing at its former location.\n\nIt is done. After months of study and research accounting for new gravitational wells and habitable zones, [Root.Capital.GetStarName] now has a new inhabited planet orbiting it.
colony.9850.desc.hive: A formless static covers a large swath of §B[Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta's§! sky and is closing in rapidly as [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Alpha and Beta and all other available drones work side by side. The negative mass stabilizers activate, and the tear between worlds moves over [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta just as the static would smother it. The rift winks out moments later, and negative mass stops being produced at its former location.\n\nIt is done. The new perspectives and minds joining the [Root.GetName] send a ripple through the Collective. After months of study and research accounting for new gravitational wells and habitable zones, [Root.Capital.GetStarName] now has a new inhabited planet orbiting it.
colony.9850.desc.robot: A formless static covers a large swath of §B[Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta's§! sky and is closing in rapidly as [cloned_physicist.GetName]-Alpha and Beta and all other available science units work side by side. The negative mass stabilizers activate, and the tear between worlds moves over [Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta just as the static would smother it. The rift winks out moments later, and negative mass stops being produced at its former location.\n\nIt is done. After months of study and research accounting for new gravitational wells and habitable zones, [Root.Capital.GetStarName] now has a new inhabited planet orbiting it.
colony.9850.name: Elation!
colony.9851.desc: Probes left in the Beta universe record the final moments of reality, as a formless static wall absorbs first [Root.Capital.GetStarName]-Beta and then §B[Root.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta§!. The feed is abruptly cut off shortly before the rift winks out of existence. The negative mass particles it was producing are likewise gone.\n\nAnyone left on that side is no more.
colony.9851.name: Static
colony.9855.b: They should stay on their side.
colony.9855.desc: A common issue has started occurring ever since the rift appeared. Families in our dimension are reaching out to their Beta counterparts and smuggling them into our stable universe. This is often done by the border guards assigned to keeping the universes separate, as basically everyone in the [Owner.GetName] has family on the other side. A few groups doing this wouldn't matter, but we would quickly have a stampede on our hands if the practice spreads. If §B[Owner.GetHomeWorldName]-Beta§! loses too many inhabitants, their infrastructure will collapse, and it will be even harder to get the world through.
colony.9855.name: Crossing the Dimensional Border
colony.9860.a: Return the great work and apologize profusely.
colony.9860.desc: One of the great things about having a mirror world so near is that [Owner.GetSpeciesName] cultural pillars that might have been destroyed or lost in the last few years might still exist on the other planet, so everyone can enjoy them again. Yet unsavory characters have taken this as an opportunity to infiltrate §B[Target.GetName]-Beta§! and secure these great works for themselves. We now possess not one but two masterworks made by a great inventor from our past. [Target.GetName]-Beta's government has already sent an angry yet formal request for us to return the plunder.
colony.9860.name: Mission: Dimensional
colony.9870.a: Redouble our efforts, we can't let it end here.
colony.9870.a.tooltip: The §Y$approach_save_b_world$§! approach will require even more of our scientists, reducing our research speed by a total of §R-30%§!
colony.9870.b: All is going according to plan.
colony.9870.c: They are [Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] too, we can't let it end like this!
colony.9870.desc.helped: The situation in the Beta-Universe is dire, and it's only getting worse. A unified cry for salvation was heard from the portal earlier this morning. Even with our best efforts, it seems like our kin will become one with the nothingness haunting their universe. If we want to save our alter selves, the time is now.
colony.9870.desc.ignored: A pitiful cry for help was heard from the Beta-Universe portal today, a final whimper for salvation. We have been benefiting from their situation for a while, yet they still call out to us since there is no one to talk to in their lonely universe. We are approaching the point of no return. Soon, the Beta-[Owner.GetSpeciesNamePlural] will be no more.
colony.9870.name: One Last Plea
colony.9875.b: They need all the [Owner.GetTeamMemberPlural] that they can get.
colony.9875.desc: Having a second [Owner.GetGovernmentName] which is so similar provides us with an unprecedented opportunity. The calculations required to keep our consciousness organized every day take up many [Owner.GetTeamMemberPlural], but this task can now be offloaded to the second [Root.GetName]. The value of this is apparent, and while it might slow down the recovery effort of §B[Target.GetName]-Beta§!, we are sure we will still manage.
colony.9875.name: Offloading Optimization
colony.9880.a.hive: Defeat the divergences, suppress the Beta-World.
colony.9880.a.tt: Gain §Y400§! defensive armies at the cost of §R100§! £pop£ §HPops§!.
colony.9880.b: Analyze why the Beta-Universe reacted like this.
colony.9880.desc: In their continued distress, the other [Owner.GetGovernmentName] has lashed out and manically taken a hold of the [Owner.GetSoldierPlural] on [Target.GetName]! We must organize our defense drones before we are overrun.
colony.9880.name: Desperate Drones
colony.9885.a.hive: We will make sure that you do.
colony.9885.a.hive.tooltip: Suppress the presence of the Beta-World hive mind through our superior numbers.
colony.9885.a.machine.tooltip: Ensure that the other dimension does not have any more unsecured connections to [FromFrom.GetName].
colony.9885.b.machine: Understandable, combat AI is subversive by nature.
colony.9885.desc.hive: The final divergent drone has been defeated. Our communication drones are once again detecting the presence of the other Overmind, but it's acting a lot submissively this time, waiting for us to initiate communication.\n\n"§BThis Mind apologises - instinctive reactions are getting harder to suppress as §RThe Static§! nears. We will ensure that we restrain ourselves in the future.§!"
colony.9885.desc.machine: The rebelling defense unit has been defeated. Our observation analysis subroutines are once again detecting the presence of [FromFrom.GetName]-Beta's communication units. They left us with a simple message.\n\n"§BOnce again redundant defense units have acted in sub-optimal ways. As the §RThe Static§! approaches, they managed to get through our quarantining efforts. The processes have since been deleted and should not take any further action.§!"
colony.9890.desc: [FromFrom.GetName] has fallen to our Beta variants. They are now demanding the immediate transferal of some of their drones as well as the establishment of a sub-consciousness on our world to ensure the survival of their knowledge and existence.
colony.9890.name: Demands
colony_fed.100.desc: A geological anomaly has come to our attention on [Root.GetName]. We began surveying after a bowl-shaped depression suddenly appeared alongside a mining facility there. Features like this are almost never found outside of a glacial region, but stranger still: the walls of this 'cirque' scatter visible light in a flower-petal pattern, and have been found to resonate when exposed to certain electro-magnetic bands. Investigations are ongoing.
colony_fed.100.name: Impossible Corrie
colony_fed.105.a: Bring it back into the fold.
colony_fed.105.b: Let's see where this research goes.
colony_fed.105.desc: Our scientists report that the newly-uncovered, crystalline blue deposits on [Root.GetName] respond dramatically to delayed-erasure photon energy. The minerals filter its wavelengths and reflect a beam which is capable of transforming ordinary silicates into a new, super-conductive alloy - though only ever during daylight.\n\nGiven that this process essentially involves bouncing high levels of radiation around an enclosed space, some scientists have already come out in protest. A different group of excited researchers offers a counter-argument, stressing that this phenomenon could revolutionize the way we refine precious metals. Either way: developing this technique further will be costly.
colony_fed.105.gestalt.desc: A rogue drone has been found running its own project within the cirque on [Root.GetName]. Driven by its initial directive - to refine our methods of mineral extraction - it has since stumbled onto a means of transforming everyday silicates into a new type of alloy.\n\nThe process seems to involve bouncing high-energy beams off mineral deposits in the feature's wall. The drone's eagerness in its task has caused it to flood the area with excessive levels of radiation. It has therefore been isolated pending either re-integration, or destruction of its individuality and acquired knowledge.
colony_fed.105.name: Project Blue Lotus
colony_fed.106.desc: Regrettable scenes on [Root.GetName], as a group of obsessive scientists sought to intervene in the project's closure. Dazzled by their own research, they attempted to wrest control of the transmutation experiments 'for the benefit of new science.' The resulting scuffle caused equipment to be damaged, and a runaway cascade took hold.\n\nWhat remains of the cirque is something akin to a geode: a rocky shell around what used to be the equipment and protestors, now re-rendered in crystalline form.
colony_fed.106.name: Overly-Keen Proponents
colony_fed.107.desc: The wayward drone and its findings have been successfully purged. The results of its fluke experiments now litter the landscape; a small amount of useful material has been reclaimed.
colony_fed.107.name: Breakaway Alchemist
colony_fed.110.desc: The laboratory on [From.GetName] is yielding verifiable results. Although their process can still only transmute small amounts of rock into alloys, researchers have high hopes for a larger-scale operation. They have requested access to further resources.
colony_fed.110.gestalt.desc: The rogue experiments on [Root.GetName] are yielding results. Although the process can still only transmute small amounts of matter into this new metal, the experiment is now verifiable. This could warrant more dedicated research efforts.
colony_fed.110.name: Alchemy in Motion
colony_fed.111.desc: The transmutation experiments at [From.GetName] have failed - though their failure may actually have prevented future catastrophe. When new, more refined equipment was first brought online, it ran well within design tolerances. However, when shut-down instructions were issued, the process accelerated beyond the reach of its failsafes. Conversion took hold in the facility's housing, transmuting it and its surroundings into the same, super-conductive alloy.\n\nThe resulting ground explosion has taken a number of lives along with significant chunks of the surrounding landscape. We're left with little other than a seam of good material, and a cautionary tale in metaphysics.
colony_fed.111.name: Lotus Collapse
colony_fed.115.desc: The next phase of our experimental production facility has come online. The Blue Lotus crystalline transmutation facility is now busy converting unprecedented amounts of base material into useful alloys.
colony_fed.115.name: Full Spectrum Alchemy
colony_fed.120.desc: A catastrophic failure has occurred at the experimental facility on [Root.GetName]. Operatives say we may never know what specifically caused the failure in containment, but the result was runaway transmutation of the equipment, its housing, and a vast chunk of the surrounding landscape - all into the same, superconductive alloy. A rich seam of this material is all that remains.
colony_fed.120.name: Lotus Eats Itself
colony_mod.1.a: Let's get to the bottom of this!
colony_mod.1.desc: While it's obvious that some past calamity released a vast amount of radiation on [Root.GetName], it's not obvious what caused it. This mystery is now bothering more and more of the colonists who have made [Root.GetName] their home. After all, if we don't know how this happened, what is to say it could not happen again?
colony_mod.1.desc_mach: While it's obvious that some past calamity released a vast amount of radiation on [Root.GetName], we have yet to determine its cause or whether it is likely to happen again.
colony_mod.1.name: What Happened Here?
colony_mod.10.desc: The atmosphere of [Root.GetName] has been cleansed of its intoxicating elements!
colony_mod.10.name: Crackdown
colony_mod.101.desc: After a period of research and study, the scientists on [Root.GetName] have managed to make a breakthrough and achieve limited communications with some of the Titans. While huge, slow, and difficult to talk to, the Titans are incredibly tough and strong. Some few have expressed a desire to join our military forces, where they will undoubtedly be an incredible asset.
colony_mod.101.name: Titanic Life Study: Success
colony_mod.102.desc: In a disastrous series of events, the scientists on [Root.GetName] have enraged the indigenous Titanic Life. Huge creatures are rampaging across the colony, smashing everything in their path.
colony_mod.102.name: Titanic Life Study: Failure
colony_mod.11.desc: The atmosphere of [Root.GetName] has been filtered to greatly reduce the effects of the hallucinogen.
colony_mod.11.name: Crackdown: Breakthrough
colony_mod.16.desc: The Strong Magnetic Field around [Root.GetName] has been affecting computers on the surface recently. Oddly, this effect is not merely random interference, instead computers are actually working more efficiently than they should be. It's almost as if an outside force is lending a helping hand...
colony_mod.16.name: Magnetic Miracle
colony_mod.17.desc: The Strong Magnetic Field around [Root.GetName] has always caused some problems with electronic instruments on the surface, but recently the effect on our computers has been especially notable. So far, it is unknown what has caused this flare up, although we suspect it to be temporary.
colony_mod.17.name: Magnetic Disruption
colony_mod.18.desc: [Root.GetName] is the site of a self-organizing quantum computer of astounding complexity and subtly. The patterns of the weather, the native life, even our own colony is incorporated into it and somehow used as neurons in a planet-sized network. We do not understand how this is possible, and we have no way of controlling it, but we do know that if we arrange our computers in a certain way [Root.GetName] will enhance their performance.
colony_mod.18.name: Magnetic Mystery Revealed
colony_mod.2.c: Ensure that the research does no harm.
colony_mod.2.d: Study them? Harvest them and see if anything is useful!
colony_mod.2.desc: The native life of [Root.GetName] is built on an epic scale, far larger than anyone previously thought was possible for biological life. The question now in the minds of our researchers is "What is their secret, and can we benefit from it?" Proposals to study the native life in greater detail are flooding in.
colony_mod.2.name: Titanic Life
colony_mod.21.desc: The recent earthquake which shook our colony on [Root.GetName] has caused a large sinkhole to open. Whatever once occupied that spot is now deep underground.
colony_mod.21.name: Earthquake: Damage Report
colony_mod.22.desc: The recent earthquake which rocked our colony on [Root.GetName] caused no damage and, serendipitously, has uncovered a batch of useful minerals.
colony_mod.23.desc: The recent earthquake which staggered our colony on [Root.GetName] caused no damage!
colony_mod.3.desc: The unstable tectonic plates of [Root.GetName] have just violently shifted once again. Reports on the damage to the colony are just starting to arrive.
colony_mod.3.name: Earthquake!
colony_mod.4.desc: The population of [Root.GetName] are currently witnessing a spectacular sight. A comet is passing through [Root.GetName]'s asteroid belt and the effect is being described as "magnificent."
colony_mod.4.name: Comet Sighted Through Belt
colony_mod.5.desc: While it cannot be denied that the intoxicating effects of [Root.GetName]'s atmosphere are enjoyable, and even helpful in some cases, there is pressure from the more conservative parts of the [Root.Owner.GetName] to crack down on the possibly addictive gases.
colony_mod.5.name: Crackdown
colony_mod.6.a: Study the impact sites for details of the weapons used.
colony_mod.6.desc: After a thorough investigation, we have come to the conclusion that [Root.GetName] was the site of an ancient genocide. As far as we can determine, the native population of [Root.GetName] was on the verge of becoming a space-faring race when a far more advanced race suddenly entered the system, bombarded [Root.GetName] from orbit, and left again, leaving the few survivors doomed to extinction.
colony_mod.6.name: Bombardment
colony_mod.7.a: Study what remains of the battlefields.
colony_mod.7.desc: After a thorough investigation, we have come to the conclusion that [Root.GetName] was a casualty in some forgotten war. Who lived here and who they fought is unknown, but it is clear that they were wiped out following an extra-solar invasion force entering the system and the ensuing battle for the planet. While this is a chilling realization, we can at least be reasonably sure that it is unlikely to happen again.
colony_mod.7.name: Interstellar War
colony_mod.8.a: What could drive people to such a fate?
colony_mod.8.desc: The tragic history of [Root.GetName] has been uncovered. Long ago, it seems that [Root.GetName] was dominated by two competing superpowers. At some point war broke out between them and the conflict escalated until all advanced life on [Root.GetName] was eliminated by excessive use of nuclear weapons.
colony_mod.8.desc_mach: Long ago, it seems that [Root.GetName] was dominated by two competing superpowers. At some point war broke out between them and the conflict escalated until all advanced life on [Root.GetName] was eliminated by excessive use of nuclear weapons.
colony_mod.8.name: Racial Suicide
colony_mod.9.desc: Despite extensive research into the history of [Root.GetName] we just don't know what happened here. The past remains a mystery.
colony_mod.9.name: We just don't know.
communications_spread.1.desc: By intercepting a message sent to the [CommSpreader.GetName], we have learned that they are in regular contact with another spacefaring empire that we ourselves have no contact with. By tracing this message to its source, we have been able to establish our own line of communications with this previously unknown actor on the galactic stage.
communications_spread.1.name: Communications Intercepted
communications_spread.2.desc: We have received a communiqué from a previously unknown spacefaring empire that call themselves the §H[From.GetName]§!. They claim to have learned of our existence by listening in on the communications of another empire we are in contact with.
communications_spread.2.name: New Contact
cool_relic_world_site_desc: An entire planet covered in vast structures, this fallen megalopolis surely has secrets to be unearthed.
country.1.a.tooltip: Begins the Sublight Exploration Probes Event Chain
country.1.desc: Before we developed faster-than-light travel, several sublight exploration probes were dispatched from [Root.Capital.GetName] at near-relativistic speeds towards nearby systems. The scientists who developed the probes naively included sensitive information about our culture in their memory cores as a form of greeting to alien civilizations.\n\nIt has now been realized that this data could potentially be used against us. We need to track down these probes before they are found by someone - or something - unsympathetic to our species!
country.1.name: Sublight Exploration Probes
country.10.desc: The [Root.GetName] has detected a massive subspace anomaly in the [Root.GetStarName] system. It appears to be centered on one of our missing sublight probes!
country.10.name: Subspace Anomaly
country.1000.desc:
The Head of the [Root.GetName]'s Research Department has gone missing.

Along with their privately-funded, highly experimental prototype Science Ship.

The incident has the scientific community on [Root.Capital.GetName] in an uproar.
country.1000.name: Wanderlust
country.1001.a.tooltip: Begins the Wanderlust: Rogue Scientist Event Chain
country.1001.desc: The whereabouts of the Head - now technically the former Head of Research - have yet to be ascertained. Certain details regarding the prototype Science Ship and the Head's private research have reached our ears, and while some aspects seem too fantastical to be true, it is clear that it is in the [Root.GetName]'s interest to find and recover the Chair as soon as possible.\n\nThe Situation Log has been updated.
country.1001.name: Wanderlust: With Purpose
country.1003.desc: The Research Head is not in this system.\n\nEither the lead was a dud, or the trail has gone cold.
country.1003.name: Wanderlust: Dead End
country.1005.desc: The Researcher's ship is in this system - we think.\n\nWe are unable to lock in their position on sensors, but they are hailing us. Patching them through to [Root.Capital.GetName].
country.1005.name: Wanderlust: A Glimpse
country.1010.a: What is the meaning of this?
country.1010.b: We can assign ships to escort you home.
country.1010.b.response: I have no interest in returning home at present.\n\nBut please, as a token of my goodwill, take these drones. A donation to the [Root.GetName]. I found them drifting on the outskirts of this system, and only after extensive repairs did I realize that they are utterly unfit to function as research probes.
country.1010.c: You will return to the capital at once.
country.1010.c.response: I think not, this is but the beginning. Duty calls, for science, and so on.\n\nBut please, as a token of my goodwill, take these drones. A donation to the [Root.GetName]. I found them drifting on the outskirts of this system, and only after extensive repairs did I realize that they are utterly unfit to function as research probes.
country.1010.desc: Greetings and salutations, [Root.GetRulerTitle].\n\nI take it this is not a social call?
country.1015.desc: The Chair has vanished, inexplicably, yet again.\n\nHowever, they did leave a number of drones behind, as promised. The drones are armed, and their weapons are powering up!
country.1015.name: Wanderlust: The Drones
country.1020.desc:
The drones' IFF modules had been removed, likely a result of the Head Researcher's repairs, but their threat assessment processors remained intact and somewhat stressed by the Head's invasive procedures.

It is unlikely that the head meant for the drones to attack us, but fact remains that they covered the scientist's escape nicely.

Consult the Situation Log for a §YSpecial Project§! to track the Head from their last known location.
country.1020.name: Wanderlust: The Drones Destroyed
country.1022.desc:
It seems the drones left behind by the Researcher have been destroyed, by something or someone.

We should seize this opportunity to pick up the Head's trail.

A §YSpecial Project§! has been added to the Situation Log.
country.1022.name: Wanderlust: The Drones Defeated
country.1025.desc: Having decoded the intricate web of energy signatures left behind by the Chair's elusive Science Ship, we are on their trail once again.\n\nConsult the Situation Log for details.
country.1025.name: Wanderlust: Special Project Completed
country.1030.desc:
The ephemeral Science Ship remains difficult to detect, but apparently not difficult enough.

The blur of confused sensor readings that we have come to associate with the Head's ship is flanked on both sides by a pair of rather nasty-looking corvettes.

The Physicist Head is hailing us.
country.1030.name: Wanderlust: In Trouble
country.1035.b: Tell us more about this Window, first.
country.1035.c: We will try to get you out of this mess.
country.1035.desc:
Greetings, [Root.GetRulerTitle].

[Root.GetSpeciesName] ships are a most welcome sight. I fear my own sudden appearance in this system may have angered the alien beings aboard the ships that now surround mine.

Any assistance in rectifying whatever faux pas I may have committed would be most appreciated. I will gladly share with you the nature of my expedition once this matter is settled.
country.1040.desc: Get lost! We found the rotten ghost-ship first.\n\nOnce we figure out how to see it proper-like, it's as good as boarded. And ours. Not yours. And its captain dead.
country.1041.a: Pray that we do not meet again, degenerates.
country.1041.b: All things are fleeting, material wealth especially so.
country.1041.c: Money talks. Sometimes you have to raise your voice.
country.1041.desc:
150 Energy Credits? Hardly a drop in the domesti-beast's piss-bucket, ugly. But...

Bah, the filthy ghost-ship has been more trouble than it's worth anyway.

Skitskur'r! We out!
country.1041.name: Sunblaster Pirates
country.1042.a: You will know the military might of the [Root.GetSpeciesNamePlural].
country.1042.desc: The fool needs to be taught a lesson.\n\nSkitskur'r! Weapons!
country.1042.name: Sunblaster Pirates
country.1044.desc: I couldn't help but catch bits and pieces of that conversation - they were broadcasting on an open channel, after all.\n\nI gather the transaction went smoothly.
country.1044.name: Head of Research
country.1045.b: You are to return to [Root.Capital.GetName] immediately.
country.1045.desc: I see you made short work of the pirates, [Root.GetRulerTitle].\nAs a scientist, I abhor violence... But recognize that it may have been necessary in this case. I strongly suspect I would have been treated less than kindly at the hands of those pirates.
country.1046.desc:
You know I will not, [Root.GetRulerTitle].
In fact, having had some time to consider additional possibilities, I believe there is a significant risk I will not be able to return within a reasonable timeframe.

I have taken the liberty of uploading whatever research data I have that may benefit the [Root.GetSpeciesName] people to the databases on [Root.Capital.GetName]. The data related to the Window stays with me, though. I am starting to think I am not ready; certainly no one else is.
I will be going now.
country.1047.desc:
A quick check confirms the Head's claims, and the [Root.GetName] has enjoyed a small but not insignificant boost to our collective body of physics research.
